  neighbouring toast uses in running text.
- **`已加入购物车，下一批现做`** — the checkout notice's kicker, `下一批现做`,
  instead of the badge's `下批现做`. Rejected: the customer just tapped a button
  reading `下批现做`; echoing that exact string is the whole point, and the
  notice's longer form belongs to the notice.

## The verdict that had no Chinese half (2026-09-13)

Channel sync has five verdicts. Four of them shipped bilingual — `已同步`,
`待处理`, `已关闭`, `未上架` — and the fifth, `unk`, shipped as
`['Name not checked', 'Name not checked']`: English on both sides, reaching a
Chinese reader in English on three surfaces at once. The desktop's shared
`CH_STATE_WORD` (`01-core.js`), the Products page's channel dots
(`09-products.js`), and the phone's `csWord` (`m.html`).

It was not an oversight, and `01-core.js` said so in a comment: `unk` was held
English deliberately, as the placeholder the Meituan and Eleme tabs already
carry (`MT_PENDING_CN` / `EL_PENDING_CN`), *"while Ash sources the Chinese"*.
**That default is the one Rule 4's 2026-09-06 amendment repealed** — the
Chinese is delegated now — so the placeholder had outlived its own reason and
was still shipping.

**Nothing is minted for it.** `unk` is not really a verdict: per
`lib/channel-sync-items.js`, it means the item IS mapped, but the store's
catalogue has never been read, so the name cannot be checked either way — one
fact about the STORE, drawn neutral, never amber. The Channel sync page has
been stating that exact fact in Chinese on its own store lines for as long as
it has existed.

### Lifted verbatim — recorded, not composed

| where | EN | CN | from |
|---|---|---|---|
| the `unk` verdict word, all three surfaces | Name not checked | 尚未读取商品 | `29-channel-sync.js`'s store line — the same page, one panel up, where a store whose catalogue has never been read already reads `尚未读取商品` |

**The English half is the one already shipped, not the source pair's.** On the
store line the live pair is *no listings read yet* / `尚未读取商品`. Only the
Chinese half moves here; it is re-paired with the verdict word's existing
English rather than replacing it, because *Name not checked* is what five
files and two surfaces already say and this entry exists to close a gap, not
to re-word a shipped verdict. The two halves name the same fact from
different ends — the cause (the catalogue was never read) and its consequence
(so the name is unchecked) — which is what the state is.

It also sits right for the slot: the cell word renders beside
`找不到该商品` (6), `门店未关联` (5) and `未选规格` (4), so six characters is
the established shape, not an outlier.

### Rejected

- **`尚未核对名称`** — "the name has not been checked yet", a literal read of
  the English. Rejected on Rule 4's own order of preference: a live string
  states this fact on this very page, so composing a second way to say it
  would put two phrasings of one state in one product for no gain.
- **Eleme's live `尚未读取商品目录，无法匹配`** — "the catalogue has not been
  read, so nothing can be matched" (`14-eleme.js`), which carries the whole
  semantic including the consequence. Rejected on shape: this slot is a
  verdict WORD standing beside four others, and a twelve-character clause
  with a comma in it would not read as one of a set of five.
- **Restructuring the English to the source pair's own *No listings read
  yet*, so the live pair transfers whole.** This is the move CLAUDE.md
  prefers — restructure the label rather than mint a string — and it is
  rejected only because nothing is being minted here either way: taking it
  would mean rewriting shipped English across five files and two surfaces to
  avoid supplying one Chinese half, which is the larger change of the two.
- **Leaving it English, as `01-core.js` intended.** Rejected: that comment
  predates the 2026-09-06 amendment and is the default it repealed. Waiting
  is no longer the instruction.
- **Filling `MT_PENDING_CN` / `EL_PENDING_CN` at the same time.** Rejected as
  a different job: those are whole sets of ~15 English strings each
  (`catNever`, `catLabel`, `catRefresh`, `catFailed`, …), still English on
  both sides, and they remain so. This entry covers the verdict word only.

## Payment and delivery — three untaught tender words on Reports (2026-09-13)

Reports → Sales → **Payment and delivery** bars its revenue by
`retail_orders.payment_method`, through a lookup in `dashRenderSplits`
(`03-dashboard.js`). The lookup was missing three real values, and an unmapped
key there returns the raw key itself, unpaired — `meituan`, `eleme` and
`offline` were surfacing as bare English words next to properly bilingual
rows like `WeChat Pay · 微信支付`, on both languages, because a string with no
` · ` in it is not bilingual text the i18n walker can toggle.

`meituan` and `eleme` are not new vocabulary — they are the literal
`payment_method` a Meituan or Eleme channel order is written with
(`routes/meituan-internal.js:474`, `routes/eleme-internal.js:580`): money that
settled on that platform, never touching our own gateways. `offline` is the
pre-existing generic tender in `routes/retail.js`'s `ALLOWED_PAY`, the
catch-all a counter payment falls back to when it isn't tied to one of the
five specific off-app wallets (`cash`, `bank_transfer`, `wechat_offline`,
`alipay_offline`, `other`) below it.

### Lifted verbatim — recorded, not composed

| key | EN | CN | from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meituan` | Meituan | 美团 | this same file's `DASH_CHAN_SHORT` (`03-dashboard.js:974`) and `CH` (`:3125`) |
| `eleme` | Eleme | 饿了么 | this same file's `CH` (`03-dashboard.js:3125`) |

### Composed — `offline`

**THE PAIR — composed by Claude, 2026-09-13, under the 2026-09-06 delegation.**

| key | EN | CN | What it says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `offline` | Offline | 线下 | Revenue bucket for the generic counter tender — paid outside the app, no specific wallet recorded. |

The Chinese half is not new characters: `线下` is the live fragment already
standing inside the two locked pairs one row above it in the same map,
`WeChat off-app · 微信(线下)` and `Alipay off-app · 支付宝(线下)`. This entry
just gives that fragment its own bar for the one payment_method value that
predates those two and carries no wallet name to go with it.

### Rejected

- **`Other · 其他`.** `other` is already a distinct `payment_method` value one
  slot over in the same map. Reusing its Chinese for `offline` would put two
  different revenue buckets under one label, which is the exact defect this
  fix exists to close.
- **`Counter · 柜台` / reusing `Counter sale · 前台销售`** (`till.html`).
  `offline` names how the money was taken, not which sales channel it came
  through — a counter sale can be paid by any wallet, and a delivery order can
  be marked paid `offline`. Borrowing the counter-sale word would conflate the
  two.

## Was this ordered from a supplier? — the Transactions form (2026-09-13)

The one question `public/retail-admin/22-finance.js` gained under
`docs/tacet-consolidation-decisions.md` §111 part two, with the settings control that takes
its answer back. Register: OPERATOR (Rule 1) — the person recording what the business spent.

**Nothing here is a new word.** Every Chinese term in the six composed strings is lifted from
a pair already live in this product, and four of the six come off this very screen. What is
composed is the arrangement, because no screen in this product has ever asked an operator
which of two records a cost belongs in.

### Taken verbatim (no new Chinese)

`Continue · 继续` and `Cancel · 取消` — the dialog's two buttons. Both are already live in
`22-finance.js` itself.

### The live terms these are built from

| term | the live pair it comes off | where |
|---|---|---|
| `采购单` | `Open purchase order · 查看采购单` | `22-finance.js`, this screen |
| `记入` | `Posted by Purchasing · 采购单自动记入` | `22-finance.js`, this screen |
| `支出` | `Money out · 支出` | `22-finance.js`, this screen |
| `财务` | `Could not load Finance. · 财务数据加载失败。` | `22-finance.js`, this screen |
| `供应商` | `Choose supplier · 选择供应商` | `16-purchasing.js` |
| `下单` | `Place order · 确认下单` | `16-purchasing.js` |

### Composed

| where | EN | CN |
|---|---|---|
| the question | Was this ordered from a supplier? | 这笔是向供应商采购的吗？ |
| under it | A purchase order reaches Finance when you place it. | 采购单下单后才会记入财务。 |
| first answer | Put it on a purchase order | 记入采购单 |
| second answer | Record it as an expense | 记入支出 |
| the toast, for a category already answered | This goes on a purchase order | 该笔记入采购单 |
| the settings checkbox | Ordered from a supplier | 向供应商采购 |

**THE TWO ANSWERS ARE DELIBERATELY THE SAME SHAPE.** `记入采购单` and `记入支出` differ in
exactly one word — where the cost goes — because that is the only thing the operator is being
asked to decide. An asymmetric pair would read as one real option and one way out.

**The sentence under the question is a disclosure, not a reassurance, and it is the honest
half of this change.** A typed row is in the books the moment it is saved; a purchase order
posts nothing until somebody places it. So choosing the purchase order moves that money out
of the month's figures until the order goes out, and the operator is told so in the same
breath as being asked. `下单后才会` — *not until it is placed* — is the whole point of the
line; a softer wording would be the screen declining to say what it does.

**The toast fires only where the question does NOT.** A category already answered *ordered*
is not asked again — that is what the answer is for — so the screen changes under the
operator with nothing said. `该笔记入采购单` is what says it, in the same two words the
answer they once gave was written in.

### Rejected

- **`采购 · Purchase` alone for the settings label.** It names the activity, not the fact
  being flagged. The checkbox answers *is what is filed here bought from a supplier*, and
  `向供应商采购` is that sentence; `采购` on its own would read as a category of spending,
  which is exactly what it is not.
- **`这一行向谁采购？`** (`16-purchasing.js`, the line's supplier picker). Considered for the
  question, and rejected: it asks WHICH supplier, taking for granted the very thing being
  asked here. Its `采购` is the term that was taken; its sentence is a different question.
- **`采购单自动记入`, whole, as the toast.** It is the live pair the term `记入` comes from and
  it very nearly fits — but it describes what Purchasing does to the books automatically, on
  a row that is already there. Said to somebody who has just been moved to another screen it
  would be describing the wrong end of the journey.
- **`是 / 否` prefixes on the two answers.** Dropped rather than translated: the answers are
  already self-describing, and a Yes/No in front of them would make the pair read as a
  question about agreement rather than a choice between two records.

Ash should correct any of this if it reads wrong to a Chinese operator; nothing depends on
the exact phrasing.

## Managing permissions from the phone (2026-09-13)

§112 put the whole of Settings → Team on `public/m.html` — the roster, one
person, their permission matrix, the roles behind them, and adding somebody.
The phone had four sentences about Team before this and needed a screen's worth
of them.

**134 bilingual pairs, and 96 of them were already live.** Every label the
desktop's own Team tab and Roles pane ship — `固定角色 — 不可更改`,
`此处的每项更改都会在他们下次打开页面时生效。`, `无例外 — 该成员的权限与角色完全一致。`,
`额外` / `移除`, `涉及资金` / `显示金额`, `仅可使用“加库存”应用`, `拥有仪表盘`,
`恢复为该看板的默认设置`, `新角色的名称`, `会计、周末店员…`, `当前无人使用该角色，删除不会影响任何人。`
— is used **verbatim** rather than reworded for a smaller screen. Two surfaces
saying the same thing two ways is how a shop ends up unsure whether they are
the same setting. Four more were lifted after the first draft had composed
around them: `重置密码` and `新密码(至少 10 位)` (the desktop's own reset button
and prompt), `自定义` (the roster's chip for somebody who stands apart from
their role) and `用户名仅限字母、数字和 . _ -` (the route's own refusal,
`routes/backend-team.js`).

### Arrangements of live sentences — recorded, not composed

Four sentences exist on the desktop and say *where a thing is* as part of what
they say. The phone is the other place, so the clause moves and nothing else
does.

| Live (desktop) | On the phone | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `若要让该角色使用其他功能,请先在上方“成员”中开启权限强制执行,否则…` | `…请先在“成员”中开启权限强制执行,否则…` | `上方` dropped: enforcement is a tab away here, not above |
| `开启后:仪表盘是该角色在电脑上的首屏,也是手机上的“首页”标签。` | `开启后:仪表盘是该角色在手机上的“首页”标签,也是电脑上的首屏。` | the two devices swap order — you are holding the first one |
| `关闭后:该角色在任何设备上都没有仪表盘。电脑和手机都会打开…` | `关闭后:该角色在任何设备上都没有仪表盘。手机和电脑都会打开…` | same swap; the trailing sentence about the ticks below is dropped, because on the phone they are not below, they are on the next screen |
| `角色仅影响界面显示，服务端尚未强制执行 — 该开关在电脑端。` (the phone's own, until now) | `…服务端尚未强制执行。` and `…— 仅负责人可开启。` | the switch is here now; the clause naming the desktop is replaced by the one rule that still holds — only the owner may move it |

### Composed — thirty-eight pairs

**Composed by Claude, 2026-09-13, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation.** Every
Chinese character below is already in service somewhere in this product; what
is new is the arrangement.

| CN | EN | What it says |
|---|---|---|
| `强制执行权限` | Enforce permissions | The switch itself. `强制执行` is the desktop's own word for this setting (`开启强制权限？`, and the route's `强制执行`); `权限` is the noun it governs |
| `服务端会拒绝角色权限之外的操作。您始终保留完整权限。` | The server refuses what a role does not allow. You always keep full access. | What ON means. Second clause is the desktop confirm's own `您（负责人）始终保留完整权限。` minus the parenthesis |
| `角色仅影响界面显示，服务端尚未强制执行。` | Roles shape what people see, but the server is not enforcing them yet. | What OFF means (see the table above) |
| `角色仅影响界面显示，服务端尚未强制执行 — 仅负责人可开启。` | …— only the owner can switch that on. | The same, for somebody who cannot move it |
| `已开启强制执行` · `已关闭强制执行` | Enforcing permissions · Not enforcing | The two toasts, on the live `已开启` / `已关闭` shape |
| `添加成员及更改其权限需要管理团队的权限。` | Adding somebody, and changing what they reach, needs permission to manage the team. | What is missing, on the roster |
| `更改这些设置需要管理团队的权限。` | Changing any of this needs permission to manage the team. | The same, on one person's screen |
| `修改角色权限需要设置权限的许可。` | Changing what a role reaches needs permission to set permissions. | The other capability, on the roles list |
| `设置成员权限需要“设置权限”的许可。` | Setting one person’s permissions needs permission to set permissions. | The same, on one person's screen |
| `修改此项需要“设置权限”的许可。` | Changing this needs permission to set permissions. | The same, on the matrix |
| `其他拥有“设置权限”许可的成员可以修改你的权限。` | Somebody else with permission to set permissions can change yours. | Why your own matrix is read-only — the server's rule, said as a fact rather than a refusal |
| `角色决定成员的权限。修改角色后，使用该角色的成员随之变更。` | A role is what a person holds. Change one and everybody on it moves with it. | The roles list's one line |
| `角色是一组权限。可在“角色”中修改其权限，添加后也可为个人设置例外。` | A role is a bundle of permissions… | The same fact, where an invite asks for one |
| `其权限来自所选角色。个人的例外权限在“权限”中设置。` | What they reach comes from the role. Exceptions for this one person are set under Permissions. | The role picker's own sentence |
| `该成员在角色之外的权限差异。` | What this person reaches, on top of their role. | The Permissions row's note |
| `与角色完全一致` | Exactly the role | Its value when there are no exceptions — a trim of the live `该成员的权限与角色完全一致` |
| `关闭后，其所有设备将立即无法登录。` | Switch this off and they are out of every device, at once. | Under the access switch. The live confirm says `此后无法在任何设备登录`; this is the shorter form a switch label can carry |
| `开启后，其角色权限将完全恢复。` | Switch this on and their role comes back exactly as it was. | The other direction, on the live `其角色权限将完全恢复。` |
| `店内对其的称呼。登录用户名不变。` | What the shop calls them. Their username does not change. | Why a display name is not a login |
| `请先输入姓名` | Enter a name first | Its refusal, on the live `请先填写` / `请输入` shape |
| `设置后即可使用新密码登录，原密码立即失效。` | They can sign in with it straight away. Whatever they had stops working. | What resetting a password costs |
| `密码已设置` | Password set | Its toast |
| `角色已更改` | Role changed | The role picker's toast, on the live `已更改` shape |
| `其权限适用于所有门店。` | Everything they can reach, in every store. | What All stores means |
| `仅可见下方勾选的门店。` | They only see the stores ticked below. | What it means switched off |
| `负责人始终拥有完整权限，不可缩减。` | Owner always has full access. It cannot be narrowed. | The matrix's locked footer — the live owner sentence with the desktop's `不可重命名、缩减或删除` reduced to the one verb that applies here |
| `未选择成员。` | Nobody is open. | A person screen with no person — reachable only by a route restored from history |
| `添加成员后即可登录，并按所选角色获得权限。` | Add someone and they can sign in straight away, with the role you give them. | The empty roster, which used to say people are invited on a desktop |
| `暂无可分配的角色 — 请先在“角色”中创建。` | No roles to give yet — make one under Roles first. | An invite form with nothing to give |
| `用户名仅限字母、数字和 . _ -。这是其登录账号。` | Letters, numbers and . _ - only. This is what they sign in with. | The route's own rule, plus the clause that says what a username is for |
| `至少 10 位。添加后会再显示一次。` | At least 10 characters. You will see it once more after they are added. | The password field's hint, on the live `密码至少 10 位` |
| `请把这两项告知对方。密码不会以可读形式保存，无法再次查看。` | Tell them these two. The password is not stored anywhere you can read it again. | The credential receipt. There is no invite email in this product: somebody has to be told |
| `再添加一位` · `返回团队` | Add another · Back to the team | The two ways off that receipt |
| `没有保存成功。未添加成员。` | That did not save. Nobody has been added. | The create's failure, on the live `没有保存成功。数据没有变化。` shape — the second clause names what did not happen |

### Rejected

**`许可` is used for the CAPABILITY and `权限` for what it grants, in exactly
three sentences, and nowhere else.** `修改角色权限需要设置权限的权限` is what the
plain reading produces, and a sentence that ends in the same noun twice reads
as a typo rather than as a rule. The three sentences that name the
`team:permissions` capability itself take `许可`; every other line on these
screens keeps `权限`, which is what the rest of the product says.

**`报错` / `失败` for the create refusal — rejected.** `没有保存成功。未添加成员。`
follows the live pair one clause at a time, and its second clause answers the
question a merchant actually has after a failed invite: whether somebody now
exists half-made.

**A new word for an exception — rejected twice.** `与角色有差异` was composed for
the Permissions row and thrown away in favour of `自定义`, which is the chip the
desktop roster already puts on the same person for the same reason. `差异` and
`不同` are both already in service (`与该角色有 N 处不同`) and a third word for one
idea is how two screens stop describing the same thing.

**Naming the person in the password prompt — rejected.** `新密码 for X` was
composed and dropped: the sheet opens over that person's own screen, which
carries their name in the header, and the desktop's live `新密码(至少 10 位)`
already says the only thing the prompt has to.

## Not arrived yet — the claim that becomes an order (2026-09-13)

The one question `public/m.html`'s expense form gained under
`docs/tacet-consolidation-decisions.md` §114, and the marker the approver's queue gained with
it. Register: OPERATOR (Rule 1) — shop staff on their own phone, and whoever approves what
they send.

**Nothing here is a new word.** Three of the four pairs are arrangements of terms already live
in this product, and the fourth is taken whole.

### Taken verbatim (no new Chinese)

`Open purchase order · 查看采购单` — the link on an approved claim's row. It is already live in
`22-finance.js` for exactly this jump: a ledger row that belongs to a purchase order offers
the same words to reach it. A claim on an order has no ledger row of its own, so this is the
only way to read what it cost, and it should not be a second way of saying the same thing.

### The live terms these are built from

| term | the live pair it comes off | where |
|---|---|---|
| `到货` | `Arrives · 到货` | `16-purchasing.js`, and the phone's own receiving screen |
| `尚未` | `Not on any purchase order yet. · 尚未出现在任何采购单中。` | `18-materials.js` |
| `记入采购单` | `this claim is on a purchase order — cancel that order instead · 该笔已记入采购单 — 请取消该采购单` | `routes/staff-expenses.js`, `ERR.onOrder` — **re-anchored 2026-09-17, see below** |
| `门店` | `Shop · 门店` | the expense form itself |

### Composed

| where | EN | CN |
|---|---|---|
| the phone's opt-in | Not arrived yet | 尚未到货 |
| the line under it, when ticked | It goes on a purchase order · the shop tracks it until it arrives | 将记入采购单 · 到货前由门店跟进 |
| the approver's meta line, before deciding | goes on a purchase order | 将记入采购单 |

**THE OPT-IN HAS NO OPPOSITE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** There is no *it has arrived* chip,
because unticked has to go on meaning exactly what this form has always meant — every claim
ever submitted was for goods in hand. A pair of chips would need a default, and a default here
would change what those rows say. (`已到货` IS live one screen over, on receiving, where it
means something else entirely: *N arrived*. The suite counts the commands rather than the
characters so the two cannot be confused.)

**THE SECOND STRING IS THE ONE THAT EARNS ITS KEEP.** Ticking the opt-in makes two optional
fields required — the shop and the description — and a form that started refusing things with
no explanation would be the screen keeping a secret. `将记入采购单 · 到货前由门店跟进` says
what the tick did and why the shop is now being asked for.

**THE APPROVER'S LINE IS THE SAME SENTENCE IN THE FUTURE TENSE, MINUS THE HALF THEY DO NOT
NEED.** `将记入采购单` sits on the meta line beside whose money it was, because approving a
claim normally writes a ledger row and nothing else — an approver who was not told would find
a purchase order in the buying list with no idea where it came from.

**`记入采购单` RE-ANCHORED, 2026-09-17 — AND THIS IS THE GUARD WORKING, NOT A WORKAROUND.**
These two strings were declared against v1.70's `This goes on a purchase order · 该笔记入采购单`,
the toast §111 part two showed when a category had already been answered. **§160 withdrew that
mechanism and the toast went with it**, and this section's own suite case caught it the same
hour — which is the entire reason Rule 4 asks a composition to name its source. The term is
NOT orphaned: `该笔已记入采购单 — 请取消该采购单` (`ERR.onOrder`, `routes/staff-expenses.js`) is
live, is older than these compositions, and is the string §114's own refusal at v1.81 already
lifted its first half from verbatim. The anchor moves there. **Nothing is re-worded**: both
composed strings are unchanged on screen, and the CN they are built from is the same four
characters in the same order, read off a pair that is still in the tree. Had no live source
survived, the correct move would have been to re-word these two against one that had — never
to drop the assertion, which is the only thing standing between a lifted term and a silent
orphan.

### Rejected

- **`在途采购`** (from `Nothing on the way · 暂无在途采购`, the purchasing screen). The best
  candidate considered, and the closest in meaning — *purchases in transit*. Rejected for the
  phone because it names a CATEGORY of orders, which is what that screen's empty state is
  about; the person tapping this chip is saying one thing about one purchase, and `尚未到货`
  is that sentence. Recorded so the search is not repeated.
- **`待收货`** — *awaiting receipt*. Not live anywhere in this product, and it describes the
  shop's side of the transaction rather than the fact the employee is reporting.
- **Reusing the receiving screen's `已到货` inverted.** See the note above: the same characters
  are live one screen over meaning *N arrived*, and borrowing them for a question about one
  purchase would put one phrase on two jobs.

Ash should correct any of this if it reads wrong to a Chinese operator; nothing depends on the
exact phrasing.

## The customer section on the phone (2026-09-13)

§116. Ash: *"customer section on the mobile should be fully functional like the
pc version."* Twelve gaps against `public/retail-admin/08-customers.js` — three
filters that asked a narrower question than the desktop's, six writes the phone
had no way to make, two blocks it rendered nothing for, and four buttons offered
to every operator regardless of what they may do.

**Most of this needed no new Chinese at all.** The desktop's own customer drawer
already ships the wording for referring, the ongoing share, the address form's
refusal and the note field's prompt, and this uses those characters unchanged —
the §112 rule, for the §112 reason: two surfaces saying the same thing two ways
is how a shop stops being sure they are the same control.

### Lifted verbatim — recorded, not composed

Each of these is `08-customers.js`'s own string, used as it stands.

### Rejected

**`了解` for the note-and-tags block — rejected.** It is the verb, and the block
is two nouns. `备注与标签` names what is in it, which is also what the two
buttons beside it say.

**`详细地址` for the `detail` field — rejected, and it is the desktop's own
mistake.** `08-customers.js` labels both the street line and the sub-address
`详细地址`, and the live refusal (`收件人、电话和详细地址都需要填写。`) means the
street one by it. Two fields with one label in a form that refuses by naming the
label is a refusal that points at the wrong box. `街道地址` and
`楼栋 / 楼层 / 房号` split them.

**`封禁推荐` for stopping a referral — rejected.** `封禁` is spent on the account
(`封禁该顾客`), and this deliberately does not touch the account — both live
confirms end by saying so. `停止推荐资格` is the desktop's word and stays.

**A new toast carrying the reissued code — rejected.** The desktop's
`新代码: XXXX` is the only place that code appears, and a toast is gone in three
seconds. The phone's re-read puts it on the record, where it can be read twice.

**`性别未知` for the blank gender — rejected.** It states a fact about the
customer; the field is empty because nobody asked. `— 未知 —` is the desktop's
own option text and says the same thing about the FIELD.
## Which day the batch row means (2026-09-13)

The verb the phone's Orders list gained on a fresh-batch row. Register: OPERATOR (Rule 1) —
shop staff scanning the list on their own phone.

**Nothing here is a new word.** One of the two is already shipping verbatim on this very plan;
the other is an arrangement of the same plan's own kicker.

THE REPORT. Order TC000681, read on the list at 18:47, showed a ship-by cell reading
`Tomorrow` over `made fresh · ship Today`. Both dates are right — a batch is MADE on
`promised_ship_date` and ARRIVES on `promised_delivery_date`, and the headline prints the
second over the first. Neither was labelled, so two relative day words sat one line apart and
read as one date disagreeing with itself. The desktop's batch cell prints a kicker over the
date (`DELIVER BY`, `04-orders.js`) and the phone's own drawer tile prints the same one; the
list row is a headline and a sub-line under a 52% cap with no kicker, and so had nowhere to
say which day it held.

### The live terms these are built from

| term | the live pair it comes off | where |
|---|---|---|
| `送达` | `Deliver by · 送达时间` | this same batch plan's kicker, in `m.html`'s drawer tile and `04-orders.js` |
| `发货` | `made fresh · ship Today · 现做 · 今天发货` | this same plan's own sub-line, one line below |

### Composed

| where | EN | CN |
|---|---|---|
| the row, when the batch has a delivery estimate | Arrives Tomorrow | 明天送达 |
| the row, when it has none | Ship Today | 今天发货 |

**THE SECOND IS A VERBATIM LIFT IN CHINESE AND A COMPOSITION IN ENGLISH**, which is why it is
in this table rather than the one above. `今天发货` is already on screen: it is the tail of
`现做 · 今天发货`, the sub-line this same plan prints directly beneath. The row that has no
delivery estimate has no such sub-line to print it in (its sub is the bare `现做`), so the
same two characters do the job one line higher.

**THE DAY WORD IS NOT PART OF THE PAIR.** `明天` / `今天` / `昨天` / `9月14日` come from
`fmtDateOnly`, which already mints them everywhere on this screen against the shop's clock.
What was composed is the ORDER — a Chinese time phrase leads, so `明天送达`, not the
`到货 9月14日` shape the purchasing rows use.

**BOTH SHAPES ARE LABELLED, not only the confusing one.** Labelling the two-date row and
leaving its no-estimate sibling as a bare `今天` would put a described day word on one batch
row and an undescribed one on the next, which is the same question asked again.

### Rejected

- **`到货`**, off `Arrives · 到货` (`16-purchasing.js`, and the phone's own receiving screen).
  The closest match to the English word, and the first choice. Rejected because it is the
  PURCHASING side's word — goods arriving at the shop, from a supplier — and this row is about
  an order reaching a customer. `送达` is what this very plan already calls that, one screen
  over, in its own kicker. Recorded so the search is not repeated.
- **`预计到货`**, off `Expected arrival · 预计到货` (`16-purchasing.js`). Same crossed concept,
  plus a word for *estimated* the English half does not say, in a cell capped at 52% of the row.
- **`送达时间`** — the kicker taken whole. It is a LABEL expecting a value beside it, which is
  exactly what a kicker is and exactly what this row has no second line for. `明天送达时间`
  is not a sentence.
- **Leaving the row bare and adding a kicker to it instead.** The honest alternative, and the
  one the desktop took. Rejected for this screen: the cell is right-aligned under a 52% cap
  beside the shipping city, and a third line there is the width the city loses.

Ash should correct either of these if it reads wrong to a Chinese operator; nothing depends on
the exact phrasing.


# AMENDMENT — What do you need to do? The questions above the Operations list

**§118, decided by Ash 2026-09-13.** More gains a strip of seven plain questions above the
Operations heading, each routing to the screen that answers it. The twenty-two rows are not
renamed, regrouped or reordered — option A, which would have done that, is still undecided.

**A question renders its destination's label by READING THE MORE ROW**, so the second line of
every question is a string this document already governs and none of it is declared here. What
is declared below is the questions themselves, the heading, and the collapse control.

**One rule shapes the whole set: `收货` is not spent on a question.** It is the string
`Receiving` and `Receive delivery` already collide on (see the options document §1 — both row
labels, both screen titles, and three in-screen buttons). A question built from it would ask
the operator to tell apart the one pair the strip exists to separate, so both arriving-goods
questions name their SOURCE instead — the supplier, or the other shop.

## Taken whole

| English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|
| I need more stock here | `需要补货` | `Restock needed · 需要补货`, the awaiting-restock line in `public/m.html`. Taken whole, not composed — the phrase already says exactly this |

## Copied, minus a noun

| English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Hide ▴ | `收起 ▴` | `Hide the work ▴ · 收起明细 ▴`. `明细` is dropped because there is no detail here to collapse — the questions are the thing |
| Show ▾ | `查看 ▾` | `Show the work ▾ · 查看明细 ▾`, the same pair. The ▴▾ convention is that pair's too |

## Lifted — every character off a live pair

| English | Chinese | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| Something arrived from a supplier | `供应商的货到了` | `供应商` is live in 62 places; `货到了` off the `到货` family (`Arrives · 到货`, and `尚未到货` on the claim) |
| Something arrived from another shop | `其他地点发来的货到了` | `其他地点发来的货` is VERBATIM from this screen's own empty state — `Deliveries from another location show up here. · 其他地点发来的货会显示在这里。` The strongest source in the set: it is already this screen's word for this thing |
| The kitchen needs to make something | `需要厨房制作` | `厨房制作` off the row label `Kitchen queue · 厨房制作队列`, minus the queue |
| Something needs buying from a supplier | `需要向供应商采购` | `采购` off `Purchasing · 采购`; `供应商` as above. `向供应商` is the half that separates it from asking another shop |
| Something got thrown away | `有东西损耗了` | `损耗` off `Record waste · 记录损耗` and the `Waste · 损耗` row |
| I paid for something myself | `我个人支付了费用` | `个人支付` is VERBATIM from the expense screen's own `My own money · 个人支付`; `费用` off `Expense · 费用申请` |

## Composed — one string

| English | Chinese | Built from |
|---|---|---|
| What do you need to do? | `你需要做什么？` | The only string here with no phrase behind it. `你` rather than `您` because the nearest screen in this family uses it — `What you have sent · 你提交的记录`, on the expense screen these questions lead to |

## Rejected

- **`收货` for either arriving-goods question.** The whole reason the questions name their
  source. Recorded at length above.
- **One question, `有货到了`, opening a chooser.** What the options document expected, and what
  the build rejected: the chooser's two entries are the two rows, which both read `收货`, so the
  pick would be between two identical strings. Asking twice costs nothing and puts the
  distinction in the words somebody is reading at the moment they need it.
- **`报销` for the out-of-pocket question.** The obvious word for *reimbursement*, and **not
  live anywhere in this product**. `个人支付` is, on the screen this question opens, and using
  the app's own word beats using the better-known one.
- **`需要采购` for the buying question.** Drops `向供应商`, which is the only thing separating it
  from asking another shop to send stock — the exact pair §2 of the options document lists as
  confusable.
- **`您需要做什么？`** — see the composed note. The two pronouns are both live in this file (21
  `你`, 16 `您`); the tie is broken by the neighbouring screen, not by counting.
- **A question per row.** Twenty-two questions is a second menu in a worse order. Seven, chosen
  from the five confusable clusters plus the two rows that are hard to find.

Ash should correct any of this if it reads wrong to a Chinese operator; nothing depends on the

**§119, decided by Ash 2026-09-13.** Two of option A's four renames are adopted; the
grouping, the pills and the `Invoices` rename are not. The full argument and the extent of
the defect are in `docs/tacet-consolidation-decisions.md` §119.

**The rule this whole section serves: `收货` is not the defect.** It is correct for
supplier receiving and is live in 48 places. The defect was the TRANSFER flow taking it as
its name, in both row labels, both screen titles and three of its own buttons. So the
supplier flow keeps `收货` untouched and only the transfer flow is renamed.

| English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|

## Lifted

| English | Chinese | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|

Needed because this control goes back one STEP, not to the screen: labelling it with the screen's name would have put one label on two destinations |

| Was | Is | Chinese |
|---|---|---|
| Receiving | **Receive from a supplier** | `收货`, unchanged |
| Back to Receiving | **Back to deliveries** | `返回收货`, unchanged. `deliveries` is that screen's own live English noun — `Could not load deliveries. · 无法加载收货记录。` — and *Back to Receive from a supplier* is not a sentence |

## Rejected

- **Renaming `Invoices` to *Issue tax invoices*.** Option A proposed it as an interim and it

  `Invoices · 发票`.
- **`供应商收货` for the supplier row.** The symmetrical-looking answer, and it would have
  changed a Chinese label that was never wrong, across 48 sites' worth of established
  vocabulary, to solve a problem that only existed in the other row. Rejected so the
  search is not repeated.
- **`调拨` alone for the transfer row.** *Transfer*, without saying what you do with it.

# AMENDMENT — Operations in eight groups, and the three pills

**§121, decided by Ash 2026-09-13.** The last open part of option A. Eight headings replace
the single `Operations · 运营`, and three pills carry what a row label cannot.

**Not one string here is composed.** The headings name jobs this app has always done, so the
words for them were already live; the pills are row labels or their stems. Where a job needed
two words, the heading is two live labels joined by `与` rather than a new phrase.

## The eight headings

| English | Chinese | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| Take an order | `接单` | `New orders can arrive at this store again. · 这家门店可以重新接单。` |
| Money and numbers | `营收与数据` | `营收` off `Revenue (all channels) · 营收（全渠道）`; `数据` is live in 43 places (`实时数据`, `数据未变动`) |
| Send it out | `拣货与配送` | Its own two rows: `Pick · 拣货` and `Delivery settings · 配送设置`. The heading names its contents |
| Stock coming in | `入库` | `in · 入库`, and `到货时清点入库` on the transfer screen |
| Making things | `生产` | `Record what was made · 登记生产批次` |
| Ask someone else | `发起申请` | `发起` off `This account cannot raise purchase requests. · 此账号无法发起采购申请。`; `申请` off the three request rows |
| Record and review | `登记与审批` | `登记` (36 uses, `登记批次`, `登记损耗`) and `审批` off the `Approvals · 审批` row |
| Messages and channels | `消息与渠道` | Its own two rows: `Inbox · 消息` and `Channel sync · 渠道同步` |

**`出货` was considered for *Send it out* and rejected: it appears in no live UI pair** in this
product — only in a comment — so it would have been a new word for a screen that already has
two. `拣货与配送` says the same thing in vocabulary an operator has already read.

## The three pills

| English | Chinese | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| Ask | `申请` | The stem of all three rows it sits on: `申请补货`, `采购申请`, and `费用申请` one group down |
| Approve | `审批` | The `Approvals · 审批` row itself — the pill is the row's own word, on the row |
| Settings | `设置` | The `Settings · 设置` row at the foot of More |

**There is no fourth value, and that is the design.** A row the operator simply does wears
nothing. `Ready from the kitchen` is the row that most invites one — it is the answer to an
ask — and it deliberately has none: a value meaning *you get told* would spend the scarcity
that makes the other three legible.

## Rejected

- **`出货`** for *Send it out*. See above: not live as a UI string.
- **`报表`** for *Money and numbers*. Zero uses in this product. `数据` is live 43 times.
- **A pill reading `只读` (read-only) on Sales and Trend.** A fourth value, on rows nobody
  confuses, to say something the screens already say by having no save button.
- **`运营` kept as a ninth heading above the eight.** A heading over headings, restating the
  section the operator already navigated to.
- **Composing a single phrase for a two-word job** (e.g. one new word for *Record and review*
  instead of `登记与审批`). Joining two live labels with `与` keeps every character traceable
  to a screen, which is what Rule 4 is for.

Ash should correct any of this if it reads wrong to a Chinese operator; nothing depends on the
exact phrasing.

## The run is opened by name (2026-09-14)

§128. Ash, on the product editor's *When out of stock* control — *"right now for

gap between them is a region: an out-of-city parcel leaves after the next
restock, so a pre-order is safe, while a Guangzhou same-day order is picked off
the shelf and leaves on today's run, where there is nothing to put in the box.
The third answer closes that gap by **changing what the order is** rather than by
pretending the shelf is full — it parks as `awaiting_restock`, holding nothing,
with no delivery window and no same-day fee — so the wording has to carry two
facts at once: everyone may order, and the whole order waits.

**Every fragment used below is already live.** `全国` is the sibling option's own
first two characters. `可预订` is the pill the shop grid, the PDP, the size sheet
and the favourites page all draw. `补货后发出` is lifted whole out of the
storefront's existing out-of-stock note (`当前缺货，外地可预订，下批/补货后发出。`).
`整单` appears in twenty-odd files and `一并发货` is the checkout pre-order
notice's own verb. What is composed is the assembly, and that is what is declared.

The bracket had to change with the region: `现订现发` promises a parcel that leaves on the next run, which is true out of city and false for the shopper this option is being added for, so it becomes `补货后发出` — the same document's own words for the honest version. **Rejected:** `所有顾客可预订` (closest to Ash's own phrasing, and `所有顾客` is not live in the product editor — it would be the one minted phrase in a set of lifts, for no gain over `全国`, which the option beside it already uses for exactly this contrast); `全场可预订` (`全场` is a promotions word — it means *everything in the shop* — and this setting is per product, so it would say the opposite of what it does); `不限地区可预订` (accurate and three characters longer, and it names what is NOT restricted rather than who may order, which reads as a caveat instead of an offer) |

## The shortfall behind a cost figure (2026-09-14)

§56 as amended. Ash, choosing between two designs after
`scripts/diagnose_cost_coverage.js` measured the live database: *"version a"* —
show the figure, say next to the number that it is not accurate, and drop the
note once the catalogue is fixed.

The Finance Summary's cost-of-goods and gross-profit rows were blank from §56
(2026-09-07) until that amendment. They now carry a figure, **on one condition:
the figure never appears without the share of the period it rests on.** On the
measured window that share was 29.1%, and a gross margin of 91.6% printed alone
off it is exactly the flattering fiction §56 refused. This sentence is the
condition, so it is not a caption on the number — it is what the number ships
under.

**The shape was already solved one level down.** `public/retail-admin/09-products.js`'s
`_paMarginWarn` says this about a single product's margin drawn from an
incomplete cost, and it was locked on 2026-09-01: *"Marked 'cost is not
complete' — this percentage is drawn from a cost that is missing something, so
the real margin is lower."* This is the same fact at period scale, and its
operative half is that string's, character for character.

**It says the DIRECTION, not just the fraction.** A percentage alone leaves a
reader to work out which way the error runs. Cost missing from a period can only
push the margin UP — a shortfall always flatters — and that is the half worth a
sentence.

### Composed — declared, by Claude Opus 5, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

| Chinese | English | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| `此期间 {n}% 的营收已记录成本 —— 实际毛利更低。` | Cost recorded for {n}% of this period's revenue — the real margin is lower. | The condition under which §56 as amended lets the two rows carry a figure. **Assembled from four live pieces and introduces no word.** `此期间` is this very card's own `noCostRecorded` (`此期间未记录成本数据。`); `营收` is this card's own `revenue` label, and naming that row is deliberate — the fraction is computed against it, so the sentence points at the line it qualifies rather than at sales in general; `已记录成本` is the positive of the same card's `未记录成本数据`; and `—— 实际毛利更低。` is `09-products.js:1647` verbatim, dash included. **Rejected:** `销售额` for `营收` (live only in `public/full-circle.html`, the marketing page, and never in this admin — it would name a quantity this card does not show, where `营收` names the row directly above); a bare `此期间 {n}% 的营收已记录成本。` with no second clause (true and useless — it leaves the reader to derive which way the error runs, which is the one thing they need and the one thing §56 was amended to guarantee); reusing `noCostRecorded` itself for both states (it explains an ABSENCE and this qualifies a PRESENCE — one sentence covering both would make a period with some cost indistinguishable from one with none, which is the distinction the amendment turns on) |

### Rejected

**A dated form — rejected, and for §36 v4.113's reason rather than a new one.**
The capture cutoff is now measured (31 August 2026 — §36, *The cost capture
cutoff is 31 August 2026, measured*), so a dated sentence is no longer
impossible. It is still wrong here: the fraction is a
property of the window the operator chose, not of a fixed boundary, and a window
wholly after the cutoff can still be short. **The coverage number is the honest
statement and the date would be a second, weaker one beside it.**

**A percentage that rounds — rejected.** A window at 99.6% rounds to `100%` and
prints a sentence arguing with its own number. It floors, so the figure can
never claim more coverage than there is.

**A word for the full-coverage state — rejected, nothing is needed.** At 100%
the sentence is simply not drawn. Ash's *"once we fix manually everything you
will remove that note"* is built as a consequence of the data rather than a task
anyone has to remember: the note cannot outlive the shortfall it describes,
because the shortfall is the only thing that draws it.

**A word for the zero-coverage state — rejected, `noCostRecorded` already
holds it.** A period with no costed line at all keeps the seventh state it has
had since §56, unchanged. The amendment does not reach that case: a `¥0.00` cost
of goods would claim the goods were free, which §36 refused and §56 kept.

| Chinese | English | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|

## The purchase order is dated when it was placed (2026-09-15)

**Ash, 2026-09-15: "我想这里可以更改为下单日期，而不是到货日期。因为物品到货的时间都不一样。"**
Said twice, the second time after a session had answered around it. Register:
**OPERATOR** (Rule 1) — this is the back office's 新建采购单 wizard, not a customer
surface.

**WHAT WAS THERE.** Step one of the wizard asked for `预计到货` / *Expected
arrival* and carried the hint `超过该日期后,订单会被标记逾期。` — we will flag the
order once this date passes. One date, for the whole order.

**WHY IT HAD TO GO, and it is Ash's reason rather than a style judgement.** A
retail purchase order here routinely carries many suppliers — RPO-0037 carries
seventeen — and their goods arrive on different days. A single expected-arrival
date is therefore not a fact about the order; it is a fact about at most one
supplier in it. Worse, `isLate()` (`public/retail-admin/16-purchasing.js`) built
the `逾期` badge on exactly that date, so an order with sixteen suppliers on time
and one date passed was labelled late in full. **Rule 2 is the rule already in
this document that says why this is a defect rather than a rough edge:** an
estimate and an actual never share a label, and `到货` is the word this product
uses for goods that HAVE arrived — the list column, and the receiving screen's
own count. Hanging it on a promise was the drift.

**WHAT REPLACES IT.** The order date — `purchase_orders.date` — which is the one
date that IS a single value for the whole order, which the server has always
stored, and which the orders list has always printed under the order number. No
new column, no migration; the wizard simply stops asking the wrong question.

### Composed — declared, by Claude Opus 5, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

| Chinese | English | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| `下单日期` | Order date | The field label. **Two live pieces, no new character.** `下单` is this very file's own word for the event, live on the order page's subheading (`T('placed', '下单')`, `16-purchasing.js`) and in nine other admin files; `日期` is live in eleven (`10-extras.js` table head, `20-waste.js`, `22-finance.js`, `26-print.js`, and `开票日期` in this same purchasing file). | `每件商品的到货时间可能不同。` | Items can arrive on different days. | The hint under the box, replacing the overdue promise. **Every piece is live** — `商品` in twenty-two files, `到货` in six (including this file's own `到货` column head and `在到货并勾选收货之前` on the review step), `时间` in fourteen, `每件` in two. What is composed is the sentence. It is here because removing the old hint without replacing it leaves an operator wondering where the arrival date went; this says why there isn't one. **Rejected:** saying nothing at all (the ordinary right answer under this document's own guidance — *a numeral or a name often needs no label* — and rejected only because the field did not gain a hint, it CHANGED one, and a silently vanished promise reads as a bug); `到货时间以实际收货为准。` (composed, and it asserts a procedure — "actual receipt governs" — which is true but is the receiving screen's business, not this card's); `商品到货时间不同。` (drops `每件` and `可能`, and with them the two things that make it true: it is per item, and it is a possibility rather than a rule) |

### Reused verbatim — no new string, recorded so the search is not repeated

The wizard's two recap strips — step two's summary chip row and step three's
review line — both printed the delivery date. Left alone they would have read
`预计 —` on every new order, which is the dead-UI failure that makes a removed
field look like a broken one. Both now print the order date under the live pair
already used for it on the order page: **`下单` / *Placed*** and **`下单` /
*placed*** (`T('Placed', '下单')` and `T('placed', '下单')`). Nothing was minted
for either.

### Not done, and deliberately

**`delivery_date` is NOT deleted.** Orders already carrying one keep it: the
list's `到货` column still prints it, the order page still shows `· 预计 …` when
there is one, kitchen copies still bring theirs across, and reopening such a
draft does not blank it. What changed is that the wizard no longer MINTS one.

**`isLate()` is untouched, and it will now fire less.** An order raised from
this screen carries no delivery date, so it can never be flagged `逾期`. That is
the correct consequence of removing a date that was not true — a badge derived
from a meaningless field is worse than no badge. **The honest replacement is a
per-line expected arrival**, one per supplier, with `逾期` meaning "this line is
late". That is a larger change than the one asked for and is recorded here as
the next step rather than smuggled into it.

## Setting a count over a debt (2026-09-15)

**Reported from the floor, 2026-09-15, as a screenshot of the Products grid with
a red toast across it and the question "what this error means?".** The toast read
`库存保存失败 — HTTP 400 · recount_clears_debt`. Register: **OPERATOR** (Rule 1) —
the back office Products grid and the product editor's store matrix, both
staff-facing.

**WHAT THE OPERATOR HAD DONE, AND THE SERVER WAS RIGHT.** The shelf was below
zero. Since §84 that is deliberate: −18 is how this system says eighteen units
were sold that were never held, and it is the ONLY record they are owed — the
kitchen reads it in the morning and cooks against it. The operator stood at an
empty box, typed 0, and `routes/retail-inventory.js` refused, because 0 is a true
statement about the room that silently discards eighteen customers' claim on the
next batch. The refusal is correct and is not what changed.

**WHAT WAS WRONG WAS THAT IT COULD NOT BE ANSWERED.** The route accepts one word
— `recount_reason: 'clears_debt'`, meaning *yes, I know what I am clearing* — and
the admin had no way to send it. So that cell could not be saved from that screen
by ANY value: the box refuses a negative and the server refuses everything above
it. What the operator got instead was the raw error code, because
`paSaveStoreStock` is a hand-rolled `fetch` that built its toast from `j.error`
and threw the server's own `message` and `owed` figure away — the audit A-09 gap,
in a call site that never went through `api()`. The editor matrix was worse: it
said `库存保存失败` and nothing else, whatever the server had answered.

**WHAT SHIPS.** Both grids now put the question to the operator in words and
resend with the acknowledgement if they say yes. §46's own refusal
(`recount_reason_required` — a kitchen-mode count that has gone DOWN) is answered
through the same dialog, since a kitchen-role operator reaching this screen met
the identical dead end.

### Reused verbatim — no new string, recorded so the search is not repeated

Six of the strings needed already exist for the same two questions on the phone,
and are lifted whole, punctuation included. Lifting rather than minting is the
point: the kitchen and the back office now name the same number with the same
words.

| Chinese | English | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| `有客户订单等待` | Customer orders waiting | `public/m.html` `kqOwed()` — the §84 owed block's heading, itself locked at v1.41. The dialog's title is this pair plus the numeral and nothing else |
| `数量变少了` | The count has gone down | `public/m.html:10429` — the §46 fork sheet, locked in this file's *Quick stock* table (2026-09-06) |
| `在架 {a}，你数的是 {b}。` | Shelf says {a}, you counted {b}. | `public/m.html:10430`, same table. **Full-width comma and full stop kept as they are there** — a lift that re-punctuates is not a lift |
| `数错了——保存 {n}` | I counted wrong — save {n} | `public/m.html:10431`, same table |
| `少了或坏了` | Something is missing or spoiled | `public/m.html:10432`, same table. Still deliberately generic: it is not a reason picker (§46) |
| `数量保持不变。请告诉负责记录损耗的人。` | The count stays as it is. Tell whoever records waste. | `public/m.html:10438`, same table |
| `请输入货架上的数量 — 0 或以上的整数。` | Enter the number on the shelf — a whole number, 0 or more. | `public/retail-admin/09-products.js`'s own list-grid validator, now also used by the editor matrix, which had no validation at all |

Paired against `清零并保存` it can only mean the owed figure, which is the thing the operator is being asked about. **Rejected:** `取消` (live, and the house default — rejected because *cancel* answers "do you want to do this?" when the question is "which of these two numbers survives?"); `保留欠数` (`欠` appears once in this product, in `欠款`, which is money a customer owes; borrowing it for units owed to a customer points the debt the wrong way) |

### Not done, and deliberately

**The route's `message` is still English.** It is good English and the right
thing in a log or a support ticket, and every other refusal in this admin reaches
the operator through `tdErrorText` the same way. What changed is that the two
strings a shop operator must ACT on are bilingual at the call site. Making the
route bilingual is a larger change than the one reported and is not smuggled in
here.

**Nothing is added to `TD_ERR`.** A dictionary entry for either code would be
dead: `tdErrorText` prefers the server's `message`, which these refusals always
send, and the only two surfaces that can reach them now answer with the dialog
above.

## A shelf that went below zero (2026-09-15)

**Found by survey, 2026-09-15, following the §84 refusal shipped earlier the same
day.** Meituan and Eleme have alerted the merchant when an order line exceeds
on-hand since 2026-09-08 — the section *The alert a channel order raises* above
is that wording. The mini app, the web store and the counter till reach the same
condition through `lib/inventory.js`'s two commits and **raised nothing at all**.
Register: **OPERATOR** (Rule 1) — a WeCom alert to the shop, same surface as the
channel alerts.

**IT IS ONLY FOR THE PRODUCTS NOBODY COOKS, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS QUIET.** A
batch-made product's debt already has a surface, and a better one:
`lib/batch-owed.js` reads `physical_qty < 0 AND is_batch_made = 1` and puts it in
front of the people who cook, on the screen they open at the start of a shift.
For those, selling past zero is the DESIGNED behaviour, so alerting on them would
fire on the ordinary case. A bought-in product — a drink, a packaged snack — is
outside that filter by design, is `strict` by default, and reached only a row
inside the dashboard's out-of-stock panel, sitting among the plain zeroes at
`<= 0`. Eighteen customers could be owed a case of something nobody had thought
to re-order, and the only place saying so was a panel nobody had opened. The two
surfaces now split the problem exactly: the owed block covers what this kitchen
cooks, this alert covers what it does not.

**THIS IS NOT THE PLATFORM SENTENCE AND MUST NOT BORROW IT.** `chStockOversold`
says `已按 0 计` / *clamped at 0* because the platform ingest REFUSES the shelf:
the line exceeded on-hand and nothing moved. Our own commit does not clamp and
must not — §84's negative is the honest record that units were sold that were
never held, and it is the only record the kitchen has. The shelf DID move, the
write was correct, and what is being reported is that somebody is now owed
something. Reporting a completed deduction as a refused one would be false.

### Composed — declared, by Claude Opus 5, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

One string. Everything else in the alert is lifted.

| key | EN | CN |
|---|---|---|
| `ownShelfBelowZero` | N line(s) took the count below zero and are now owed | N 项商品库存已为负数,有客户订单等待 |

**Three pieces, all live, and the seam between them is what is composed.**
`N 项商品` is `chStockUnmatched` verbatim, two rows up this very file.
`库存已为负数` is this product's own sentence for the condition, from the
admin error dictionary's `would_go_negative` (`该操作会使库存变为负数。`,
`public/retail-admin/01-core.js`) — the same words, moved from a refusal in the
future tense to a fact in the past. `有客户订单等待` is the kitchen owed
block's heading verbatim (`public/m.html` `kqOwed()`, locked at v1.41), which is
what makes this alert and the kitchen's own screen name the same debt the same
way. The English half mirrors `would_go_negative`'s English (*That would take the
count below zero*) for the same reason.

**Rejected:** `超卖` (oversold) — rejected once already for `chStockOversold`, on
the same grounds: it is the natural term, it appears nowhere in this product, and
it would be a new word for a reader who has one. **Rejected:** reusing
`chStockOversold` outright — it is one string less to explain and it says the
shelf was refused, which is the opposite of what happened. **Rejected:** `库存不足`
(the low-stock pair, live) — true of a shelf at 2 as well as one at −18, and the
whole point of the alert is that this one is past zero. **Rejected:** saying only
the number and letting `剩余 -3` carry it — the honest minimum, and rejected
because an alert arrives with no screen around it: the reader is holding a phone
and needs the sentence, not the column.

### Reused verbatim — no new string

| Chinese | English | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| `剩余` | (the balance, unlabelled) | `chStockWant`'s own half, this file |
| `订单` · `请检查` · the `🟠 {where} …\n{English}` shape | order · Please check | the channel alert above, and the daemons it took the shape from |
| `前台收银` | Counter till | `lib/capabilities.js` / `lib/roles.js` — the till's own capability label |

**A walk-in is named by the till, not by its channel.** `fulfillment_type =
'counter'` wins over whatever `channel` the row carries, because a cashier
reading this needs to know it happened at their counter, and the channel column
on a counter sale says `shop` or `web` depending on how the till was opened.

### Not done, and deliberately

**No clamp, and no new gate.** The counter till does not check stock before a
sale and must not: a walk-in holding the item can never be refused because a
database row disagrees with the room. This adds a voice, not a lock.

**No new log table.** The platforms write a sync-log row because their ingest
has one. Ours already writes `retail_stock_ledger` with the negative
`balance_after`, the order it belongs to and the channel that caused it. That is
the durable record; only the saying-it-out-loud half was missing.

**The owed block still cannot tell a debt from a miscount.** A counter sale of
three units that were physically on the shelf but not in the record leaves the
same −3 as three units genuinely owed, and `lib/batch-owed.js` reads both as
units to cook. That is a REAL defect and a larger one — it needs a decision
about what a counter-sale negative means before any code — so it is recorded
here as the next step rather than smuggled into this change.

## A negative has two causes, and they have opposite remedies (2026-09-15)

**Ash, the same day the alert above shipped: "why i need that wecom messgae i
dont understand we give permission to sell products that are out of stock."**
The question was about permission and the answer to that half is that products
given permission are not alerted — `is_batch_made` is filtered out. But working
the question exposed a real defect in the string locked hours earlier. Register:
**OPERATOR** (Rule 1), the same WeCom alert.

**WHAT WAS WRONG.** `ownShelfBelowZero` ends `有客户订单等待` — *customer
orders waiting* — on every path. That is true of a DELIVERY order that outran
the shelf: the customer is waiting and somebody has to make or re-order the
units. It is false of a COUNTER SALE, and the counter is the path that actually
fires.

A walk-in rings up three colas. They are in the customer's hand, the money is in
the till, the customer leaves. The shelf goes to −3 because the record said 0
and there were three. **Nobody is owed anything.** What the negative says is that
the count was wrong.

**AND THE TILL IS ALMOST THE ONLY PATH.** A bought-in product is `strict` by
default, and the hard out-of-stock gate in `POST /orders`
(`routes/retail.js`) refuses a strict line at checkout — so the mini app and the
web store cannot ordinarily reach this alert at all. The counter till has no such
gate, correctly: a walk-in holding the item can never be refused because a
database row disagrees with the room. So the wording that was wrong was the
wording nearly every alert would carry.

**WHY IT IS WORTH A SEPARATE STRING RATHER THAN A SOFTER SHARED ONE.** The two
readings have OPPOSITE remedies. *Units are owed* sends somebody to re-order
stock that is not missing. *The count was wrong* sends them to recount a shelf,
which is the actual repair. A sentence vague enough to cover both would send
them nowhere.

### Composed — declared, by Claude Opus 5, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

| key | EN | CN |
|---|---|---|
| `ownShelfMiscount` | , so it was likely counted wrong | ,可能是数错了 |

**One clause, swapped for `有客户订单等待` when the fulfilment is `counter`.
Everything around it is unchanged**, which is the point: one alert, one shape,
and the clause that names the cause.

`数错了` is a VERBATIM lift — `public/m.html:10431`, the §46 fork sheet's own
answer (`I counted wrong — save {n}` / `数错了——保存 {n}`), locked in this file's
*Quick stock* table (2026-09-06) and lifted again for the admin dialog at v1.85.
It is the phrase this product already uses for exactly this fact, and reusing it
means the till alert and the phone's recount fork say the same thing the same
way. `可能` is live in seven files (`public/m.html`, `public/cms.html`,
`lib/product-blocks-read.js`, and the purchase-order hint locked at v1.84:
`每件商品的到货时间可能不同。`). Only the seam is composed.

**`可能` is load-bearing, not hedging.** The system cannot know which of the two
it was — it sees a negative, not a shelf. A bare `数错了` would assert a
diagnosis, and an alert that asserts wrongly once is an alert nobody reads twice.
The English `likely` carries the same weight.

**Rejected:** `库存记录有误` (the record is in error) — accurate, and it names a
database rather than a shelf; the operator's next action is to go and count, so
the sentence should say counting. **Rejected:** `请盘点` (please stocktake) —
`盘点` appears nowhere in this product, and the alert already ends `请检查`.
**Rejected:** dropping the counter path from the alert entirely — considered
seriously, and rejected because a till sale that outruns the record is exactly
how a product comes to read sold-out on the web shop while sitting on the shelf.
**Rejected:** one sentence covering both causes (`库存与记录不符`, *stock does not
match the record*) — true of both and useful for neither, per the remedies above.

### Not done, and deliberately

**The delivery clause is unchanged.** `有客户订单等待` stays exactly as locked
at v1.86 for every non-counter path. It was never wrong there; it was wrong
everywhere else.

**Ash, told that §134 fixes the next order and can do nothing for the one that
prompted it: "build all and automatically deploy to live."** Register:
**OPERATOR** (Rule 1) — the order drawer's transition row, seen by office and
counter staff, never by a customer.

**NO STRING IS MINTED HERE, and that is the finding worth recording.** The new
control moves a settled order into the restock queue. The obvious label followed
the row's own `Mark …` pattern — `标记等待补货`, compounding 标记 (live in
`标记已发货`, `标记已送达`, `标记可取货`, `标记已取货`) with 等待补货. That
compound is not live anywhere, so it would have been a composition, declarable
under the 2026-09-06 amendment.

**It was not needed.** `public/retail-admin/04-orders.js` already carries the
exact pair on the card this button produces:

> `cuT('Waiting on stock', '等待补货')` — `awaitingRestockCard`

and 等待补货 is the same word behind the `awaiting_restock` status chip
(`retail-admin.html`), the mini app's order list and order page
(`miniapp/pages/orders`, `miniapp/pages/order`) and the web store
(`public/shop.html`). Five live surfaces, one word.

**LOCKED — lifted verbatim, nothing new:**

| English | 中文 | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| Hold for restock | 等待补货 | `04-orders.js` `awaitingRestockCard` — `cuT('Waiting on stock', '等待补货')` |

**THE ENGLISH IS RESTRUCTURED AND THE CHINESE IS NOT, which is the preference
order working as written.** *Waiting on stock* reads as a state; in a row beside
*Start preparing* and *Cancel + refund* the control needed to read as an act, so
the English became *Hold for restock*. The rule locks the Chinese, and 等待补货
serves both readings — it is what the queue is called — so restructuring the half
that is free to move removed the reason to mint the half that is not. **This is
the case CLAUDE.md describes:** *"prefer restructuring a label so an existing live
string fits it over minting a new one."*

**REJECTED, recorded so the next session does not re-open it:**

* **标记等待补货** — a composition; unnecessary once the button stopped needing to
  echo the `Mark …` pattern, which three of the row's five controls
  (`开始备货`, `退款`, `取消并退款`) do not follow either.
* **暂缓备货** (*hold off preparing*) — invented, and it describes what the
  operator stops doing rather than what the order is now waiting for. The queue is
  named for the wait, not for the pause.
* **待补货** — live, but as the SHORT form on the packing badge and the parcel
  pill (`待补货 — N 项`), where space is tight. The drawer's transition row has
  room for the full word the card uses, and matching the card is the point.

**The three refusal messages the route returns are English-only**, which is the
existing convention on `/api/retail-admin/orders/:id/status` — every message it
already returns (`A refund is currently being processed…`) is English. No register
question arises and nothing is locked for them here.

## The order says what it was told (2026-09-15)

§138. The order drawer gains two lines recording what the customer was shown at
checkout: that a line was sold as a pre-order, and that the order moved shop
because one was shut. Register: **OPERATOR** (Rule 1) — the back office order
drawer, beside `rerouteShortNote`, which answers the same question.

### Reused verbatim — no new string

| Chinese | English | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| `预订` | Pre-order | `computePreorderNotice`'s own `kicker_cn` / `kicker_en` (`routes/retail.js`), so the drawer and the screen the customer read name it identically. Also live in the product editor's policy picker (`广州外可预订`, `预订开始`) |

### Composed — declared, by Claude Opus 5, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

| Chinese | English | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| `改派 · 门店已关闭` | Rerouted, shop was closed | The move line. **Every piece is live:** `改派` is this admin's own word for an order changing shop, live as `改派 · 缺货` (*rerouted · out of stock*) and `手动改派` (*manually routed*) in `public/m.html` and `04-orders.js`; `门店` is the dashboard's own channel chip (`shop: ['Shop', '门店']`); `已` and `关闭` are live throughout (`关闭。没有订单需要等待制作。`, `06-delivery.js`). The `改派 · <reason>` SHAPE is lifted too — it is exactly how the live reroute note is built, so this reads as one more reason rather than a new construct. What is composed is `门店已关闭` and its pairing with that shape. **Rejected:** `原门店` (*the original shop*) — neither `原` nor `原门店` appears anywhere in this product, and it names the wrong half: the reader is looking at an order and wants to know why it moved, not what to call the shop it left. **Rejected:** `改派 · 门店休息` (*shop resting*) — `休息` is softer and is not the word the closure switch uses. **Rejected:** reusing the customer-facing store-move notice copy — it is the operator's own text from `storefront_config`, may be blank, and is written for a shopper rather than for the office. **Rejected:** no label at all, printing only the shop code — the honest minimum elsewhere in this file, and rejected here because a bare code beside an order reads as the shop that FILLED it, which is the opposite of what the field holds |

## The bind page stops asking for an address (2026-09-16)

The bind-profile page (`miniapp/pages/profile`) loses its address field. It was
a single `wx.chooseAddress` shortcut, and a customer with nothing saved in
WeChat does not get a list to pick from — WeChat opens its own create-address
form, whose chrome follows the customer's WeChat language while its region list
is Chinese-only. An English-speaking first-timer got readable buttons over an
unreadable list, at the moment before they had bought anything. The address is
collected at checkout instead, where our own bilingual picker already lives.
Register: **CUSTOMER** (Rule 1) — the mini app.

### Nothing composed, nothing lifted

The four EN/CN pairs the field used (`ADDRESS · NAME · PHONE · 地址 · 姓名 · 电话`,
`Import from WeChat · 从微信一键导入`, `Loading… · 加载中…`, and the hint
`WeChat gives us your name, phone, and full address in a single tap. ·
一键导入姓名、手机号与完整地址。`) are deleted with the control they labelled.
They are recorded here as removed, not banned: if the shortcut ever returns as a
secondary control beside a manual form, these are the strings it takes back.

### Subtracted — declared, by Claude Opus 5, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

| Before (live) | After | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `微信不会自动告诉我们您的昵称、头像和地址，请点击下方手动绑定。` | `微信不会自动告诉我们您的昵称和头像，请点击下方手动绑定。` | The page's own subtitle. It listed the three things the page bound; one of them is no longer on the page, so the list is two items and the enumerating `、` collapses into `和`. **Nothing is minted** — every character survives from the live sentence, in its original order. This is declared rather than treated as a silent edit because the resulting sentence is a string nobody locked, and an undeclared one cannot be told from a locked one by whoever comes after. **Rejected:** leaving the sentence as written — it would promise an address binding the page no longer performs. **Rejected:** rewriting it around the two remaining items (`微信不会自动提供您的昵称和头像…`) — `不会自动告诉我们` is the live phrasing and carries the page's voice; swapping it would be minting to no purpose |

The English half changes the same way and for the same reason:
`WeChat keeps your nickname, avatar and address private.` →
`WeChat keeps your nickname and avatar private.`

### Not done

**The `scope.address` shortcut is untouched on `miniapp/pages/addresses`.** There
it sits beside our own bilingual city→district picker and the manual fields, so a
customer who cannot read the WeChat list has somewhere to go. Removing it from the
bind page removes it from the one screen where it was the only option, which is
the whole of this change.


## The spec strip picks its words from what the catalogue already says (2026-09-16)

**§145. Nothing here is composed.** Every pair below was read out of the live
catalogue by `scripts/diagnose_spec_strip_labels.js`, over the 724 spec-strip
cells carried by 242 products, and is recorded with the count that earned it a
place. This is the preference order in `CLAUDE.md` — *copy a live pair, then
lift from the source, then compose* — resolving at the first step, because the
office had already written every one of these words.

**Why they are being locked at all, given that they are lifts.** The list is
what the editor will offer from now on, so a pair that is wrong here becomes
wrong on every product written after today. A lift can be as wrong as a
composition if the wrong twin is lifted — and there were twins to choose
between in almost every row. The choices are recorded so they can be read and
corrected rather than re-derived.

### The labels — ten pairs

| EN | 中文 | EN cells | 中文 cells | the twin NOT taken |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Product Type | 产品类型 | 64 | 83 | `Type` / 类型 (66 / 40) — see below |
| Net Wt | 净含量 | 163 | 200 | `Net Weight` (29), 净重 (2) |
| Origin | 产地 | 156 | 150 | 原产地 (4), 原料产地 (3) |
| Shelf Life | 保质期 | 57 | 57 | — |
| Diet | 饮食 | 29 | 29 | — |
| Form | 形态 | 28 | 28 | — |
| Use | 用法 | 26 | 26 | — |
| Category | 类别 | 18 | 14 | 品类 (6), 分类 (5) |
| Certification | 认证 | 13 across three spellings | 14 | `Certified` (4), `Certifications` (4) |
| Storage | 储存方式 | 5 | 5 | — |

Four of these — Shelf Life / 保质期, Diet / 饮食, Form / 形态, Use / 用法 —
match exactly on both sides, which is as strong as pairing evidence gets from a
count.

**`Type` / 类型 is the one rejection that is not about spelling.** It is a
second label for the same idea as `Product Type`, holding the same answers.
Offering both would continue a 130-cell split, so one had to go; the Chinese
decided it, 产品类型 (83) over 类型 (40). **The 66 cells that already say `Type`
are not touched** — this is a choice about what the editor offers next, not

§146. A staff expense claim submitted without a category can be filed by the
approver on the row being decided, and re-filed afterwards if it was already
approved — until now the only way to correct one was to void the claim and ask
the employee to send it again. Register: **OPERATOR** (Rule 1) — the approval
queue on both the admin Finance screen and the phone, and two server refusals.

### Reused verbatim — no new string, recorded so the search is not repeated

| Chinese | English | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| `未记录` | Not recorded | `public/retail-admin/22-finance.js`, where it is already Finance's own word for a category column holding nothing. The approval row draws a blank category with the SAME words the screen two clicks away uses for the same value — a second phrasing here would be a second name for one state |
| `— 选择分类 —` | — pick a category — | `public/retail-admin/09-products.js`'s own empty option, with the same em-dash framing. Also live as `选择分类` in `05-marketing.js` and `07-content-billing.js` |
| `已保存` | Saved | `public/retail-admin/01-core.js`. The toast after a re-filing is the product's ordinary save toast, because that is what it is |
| `更改` | Change | `public/retail-admin/04-orders.js`, where it already opens a picker over a value that is already set. The ledger row's link, and it reads correctly over a blank too — the category cell beside it says `Not recorded`, so the link changes it from nothing |
| `仅审批通过的申请` | only an approved claim | This route file's own `ERR.notApproved` (`routes/staff-expenses.js`), verbatim as the opening of the new refusal below |

### Composed — declared, by Claude Opus 5, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

| Chinese | English | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| `仅审批通过的申请可修改分类` | only an approved claim can be re-categorised | The refusal when something with no ledger row behind it is sent to the re-filing route. **Only `可修改分类` is new, and none of its characters is:** the sentence opens with `仅审批通过的申请` lifted whole from `ERR.notApproved` one line above it in the same object, `修改` is live across this admin (`修改记录`, `如需可修改`, `修改营业`), and `分类` is this product's own word for the thing (`选择分类`, `分类标签`). The `仅…可…` shape is `ERR.notApproved`'s own. **Rejected:** `重新分类` (*re-classify*) — `重新` appears nowhere in this vocabulary and reads as re-doing an act, while what is offered is changing a value. **Rejected:** `仅已审批的申请…` — `审批通过` is the live wording for this status; shortening it would put a second name on one state |
| `该笔已记入采购单 — 请在采购单上修改分类` | this claim is on a purchase order — set the category on the order | The refusal for a claim whose goods have not arrived: the order it raised owns the cost, under the LINE's category, so re-filing the claim would move nothing. **The first half and the shape are `ERR.onOrder`'s, verbatim** — `该笔已记入采购单 — 请` — which is the live refusal for voiding the same kind of claim, so the two read as one rule with two exits. What is composed is `在采购单上修改分类`; `采购单` is live throughout Purchasing, `上` and `修改` are live, `分类` as above. **Rejected:** merely reusing `ERR.onOrder` whole (*cancel that order instead*) — it names the wrong remedy: nobody re-filing a category wants the order cancelled. **Rejected:** a refusal that does not name a way out at all — `ERR.onOrder`'s own comment gives the house rule, that the refusal names the way out rather than merely refusing |
| `此账号无法修改费用分类` | this account cannot change an expense category | The refusal for an account holding neither `expenses:approve` nor `expenses:cancel`. **The shape and every piece are live:** `此账号无法审批费用申请` and `此账号无法作废费用申请` sit in the same object (`ERR.forbidden` / `ERR.forbiddenVoid`), so this is the third of a set rather than a new sentence — `此账号无法` verbatim, `费用` verbatim from both, `修改` and `分类` as above. **Rejected:** a generic `无权限` (*no permission*) — the two refusals beside it name the act being refused, and a reader who is told only "forbidden" goes looking for the wrong thing |
| `选择分类` | pick a category | The refusal for an EMPTY value sent to the re-filing route. **Both halves are live** — the Chinese verbatim from `05-marketing.js` / `07-content-billing.js` / `09-products.js`, the English from `09-products.js`'s own `— pick a category —` with the dashes dropped because this is a sentence rather than a menu row. Listed here rather than under *Reused* only because that pairing, as one refusal string, is assembled here for the first time |

### Not done, and deliberately

**No string was minted for the picker's LABEL, because it has none.** The control
is a `<select>` whose blank row reads `— pick a category —` and whose filled

list of categories.

**The claim form is untouched.** Making the category compulsory there was
rejected in §145 — somebody standing beside a taxi does not know the chart of
