| shop confirm title | Open X? / Close X? | 开启 X？/ 关闭 X？ | **RESTRUCTURED** from the live `在 X 开启 Y？` — the channel clause drops out because the shop is the whole unit |
| screen footer | Closing a whole channel everywhere is on desktop | 一次性关闭整个渠道在电脑端 | **RESTRUCTURED** from the sheet's live `一次性关闭整个渠道请在电脑端操作。` The footer it replaces said opening and closing a channel was on desktop at all, which the sheet above it had already stopped being true |

**Five are COMPOSED, by Claude, under Rule 4's standing delegation.** Four of
them exist because nothing in this product has ever had to say *this shop is
shut, so nothing here sells* — the state was real and had no sentence. Each is
assembled from live fragments.

| key | EN | CN | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| head, one shop shut | X is closed — no channel sells there | X 已关闭 — 所有渠道均不营业 | **COMPOSED** — live `已关闭` + live `所有渠道` (`所有渠道均已开启`, the line this one replaces) + `均不营业`, the live `营业` negated on the pattern of that same line's `均已开启`. **Rejected:** `全部关闭` — live, but it is the whole-channel phrase (`已全部关闭`) and would read as every channel everywhere, which is the opposite unit |
| head, several shut | N shops are closed — no channel sells at them | N 家门店已关闭 — 所有渠道均不营业 | **COMPOSED** — the same, with the live counter `N 家门店` (`N 家门店中 M 家营业`, the sheet's subtitle) |
| blocked-row explainer | The whole shop is shut, so every channel there is closed and none can be opened on its own. Open X under Shops on the Sales screen first. | 整家门店已关闭，因此该门店的所有渠道均为关闭状态，也无法单独开启。请先在销售页面的「门店」中开启 X。 | **COMPOSED** — live `门店已关闭` + live `所有渠道` + live `页面` + live `销售`, the Sales screen's own nav label, + the section header `门店` quoted in 「」 so it names what is on screen. **Rejected:** `店铺` — not this product's word for a shop anywhere; `门店` is used throughout |
| shop confirm, opening | Every sales channel at this shop opens, and it takes orders, pickups and counter sales again. Meituan follows within about a minute. | 该门店的所有销售渠道将开启，恢复接单、自提与门店收银。美团约一分钟内跟随。 | **COMPOSED** — live `恢复接单` (`public/m.html`, holiday mode) + live `自提` + live `收银` + live `美团约一分钟内` (`02-settings-ops.js` `门店约一分钟内恢复营业`). **Rejected:** stopping at `所有销售渠道将开启` — true and useless: the till and pickup are the half an operator is standing at the counter worrying about |
| shop confirm, closing | Every sales channel at this shop closes, the counter till stops selling, and orders route to the other shop. Orders already placed are not affected. | 该门店的所有销售渠道将关闭，门店收银台停止销售，订单将转由其他门店处理。已下单的订单不受影响。 | **COMPOSED** — live `收银台` + live `已下单的订单不受影响。` taken whole from the per-channel confirm beside it. **Rejected:** omitting the reroute clause — closing a shop moves its delivery and pickup to the other one, and an operator who learns that afterwards learns it from a customer |

**THE LAST SENTENCE OF BOTH CONFIRMS IS THE POINT OF THEM.** This switch writes
every channel at the shop *and* the shop-wide fulfilment flag — it is the
bluntest control in the app, and the screen it now sits on is a phone. Naming
the till, the pickups and the reroute is what stops *close this shop* being read
as *close this shop's website*.

**Nothing is retired** except the footer sentence restructured above.

**Ash should correct any of the five composed pairs if they read wrong to a
Chinese operator; nothing depends on the exact phrasing.**

## When a wallet yuan is counted (2026-09-18, §182)

| where | English | Chinese | provenance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Finance → Summary, under Revenue | Orders only — wallet money counts when spent, not when topped up. | 仅计订单 —— 储值在消费时计入，充值时不计入。 | **composed** by Claude, from live fragments |
| Reports → Overview, under Revenue | incl. ¥X top-ups | 含充值 ¥X | **lifted whole** from `01-core.js` |

**WHY EITHER SENTENCE EXISTS.** Finance's Revenue row is what customers paid on
orders, recognised at the sale. The Reports card is cash received, which books a
wallet top-up on the day the money lands and values gzgrocery off the stock
ledger. Both are right about their own question and they do not match for the
same window. Before §182 neither screen said which question it was answering,
and the first person to put them side by side reasonably read it as a bug.

**THE FINANCE SENTENCE SPENDS ITS WORDS ON TIMING**, not on what is in the
figure, because the channel lines directly above it already say where the money
came from. What they cannot show is *when* a wallet yuan was counted — and the
timing is the whole of the disagreement with the other screen.

**`储值` RATHER THAN `钱包`, deliberately.** `钱包充值` is live and is the act of
loading the wallet; `储值消费` is live and is the act this row counts — spending
it. The row says "spent" with the character the screen next door already spends
it with, and a reader moving between the two is not asked to learn that two
words are one thing.

**Ash should correct the composed pair if it reads wrong to a Chinese operator;
nothing depends on the exact phrasing.**

## One box of a parked order has left (2026-09-19, §188)

§187 let a parked order send the parcels its shortage does not touch, and
deliberately said nothing to the customer: the order keeps its `awaiting_restock`
status, so `firstDispatch` is never set and the `dispatched` line never fires.
That is right about the ORDER — 订单已发货 is untrue while the kitchen lines have
not been made — and it left the customer with **nothing at all**. A box arriving
unannounced, days before the rest, reads as a short delivery.

**Register: CUSTOMER** (Rule 1) — it is a notification row in the mini app.
**Rule 5 is honoured in the code, not in the words:** `shipsNothing` gates the
send, so a pickup customer and a counter sale never receive this line.

| where | EN | CN | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| notification title | Part of your order has shipped | 订单部分已发货 | **COMPOSED** under the standing delegation, 2026-09-19 — the live customer pair `订单已发货` with 部分 inserted |
| notification body | Order {no} — one of the parcels has shipped. The rest follows once the remaining items are back in stock. | 订单 {no} — 其中一个包裹已发货，其余商品待补货后发货。 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19, from live parts only |

**EVERY WORD IN THE BODY IS LIVE; ONLY THE SENTENCE IS NEW.** `订单` and
`已发货` are the customer register's own dispatched line; `包裹` is lifted from
the live operator button `标记此包裹已发货`; `待补货` is the live parcel hold pill
(`待补货 — N 项`); `商品` is the live parcel count (`N 件商品`). One verb
throughout — 发货, never 发出 — because the body says the same thing twice about
two different boxes and two verbs would read as two different events.

Rejected, and why, so the search is not repeated:

- **`分批发货`** — live, and it is exactly this concept, but it is the OPERATOR
  word for the *Ship part later* action on the drawer. Rule 1: a cross-register
  difference is deliberate. The customer is not performing a split; they are
  being told a box has gone.
- **`订单已发货`** alone — live, and the correct customer pair for the whole
  order having shipped. Using it here would tell the customer the order is on
  its way while the fresh half has not been made, which is the one thing §187
  refused to say. That refusal is the reason this section exists.
- **`部分发货`** — reads as an instruction or a state label rather than news;
  `订单部分已发货` keeps the live sentence's shape (订单 … 已发货) so the two
  notifications look like siblings in the list, which they are.

**NO PUSH, AND THAT IS A DECISION ABOUT THE CUSTOMER'S CONSENT, NOT ABOUT THE
WORDS.** A WeChat subscribe message costs one one-shot consent per send, and the
send worth spending it on is the one saying the whole order is on its way. So
these strings appear in the in-app notification list only; `ORDER_STATUS_NOTIF`
is untouched, which is also what stops the push firing for a status the order
does not hold.

**FLAGGED, NOT BUILT:** the parcel's MODE is not named — the customer is told
*one of the parcels*, not *the 陆运 parcel*. Naming it would be more useful and
every mode word is already a locked pair (`陆运`, `空运`), but the notification
body is a single sentence in two languages and the mode belongs to the parcel,
not the order. Worth doing if Ash wants it; not invented here.

## A box that went out on an order that was cancelled (2026-09-19, §189)

§187 stopped a cancel crediting the shelf with units sitting in a courier's van.
That made the count honest and told nobody: the money went back, the number was
right, and a box on its way to a person who is no longer a customer had no screen
anywhere saying so. This is the telling, and the answer to it.

**Register: OPERATOR** (Rule 1) — the shipment card in the order drawer, the
orders chip, and the Needs-you row on Home. Nothing here reaches a customer:
they have already been refunded and told the order was cancelled.

**ALMOST ALL OF IT IS COPIED.** 收回 is a live pair and it is exactly this verb
about exactly this kind of object — something the shop handed out, being taken
back — so the only composing is the two words built on it.

| where | EN | CN | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| card heading | This parcel was already out when the order was cancelled | 订单取消时此包裹已发货 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — from live `已取消`, live `此包裹已发货` (the parcel dispatch button) |
| card sub | Say what became of it. Only "it came back" puts the stock on the shelf. | 请确认其去向。仅“已收回”会把库存退回货架。 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — `退回` is the live waste-void wording for stock going back |
| button / closed pill | It came back / Recovered | 已收回 | live: `Taken back · 已收回`, `public/retail-admin/05-marketing.js` |
| button / closed pill | It did not come back / Not recovered | 未收回 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — the live `收回` negated |
| orders chip | To recover | 待收回 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — live `收回` with the live `待` of `待补货` / `待分配` |
| Needs-you row | Parcels to recover | 待收回包裹 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — the chip plus live `包裹` |
| confirm (recovered) | Put this parcel back on the shelf? | 把此包裹退回货架? | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 |
| confirm (not recovered) | Record this parcel as not recovered? | 登记此包裹未收回? | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — `登记` is the live waste verb for writing a movement down |

**WHY 收回 AND NOT 退回.** Both are live. `退回` is what STOCK does — the waste
void "puts the stock back", 库存退回 — and it is used here for exactly that, in
the confirm body and nowhere else. `收回` is what the SHOP does to a thing it
handed out, which is the coupon take-back's own sense and is the action being
asked about. One verb for the goods moving, one for the shop retrieving them;
collapsing the two would make "did it come back" and "does the shelf get it"
read as the same question, and the whole point of this control is that they are
not.

Rejected, and why:

- **`退回中`** — live, and tempting: it is the tracking status *Returning to
  sender* on this very screen. It names a parcel the CARRIER is already
  returning, which is one way a box comes back and not the only one, and it is a
  state the system observes rather than a question it is asking. A control
  labelled with an observed state would read as a claim about where the box is.
- **`召回`** — recall, in the product-safety sense. Wrong register entirely and
  frightening on an order screen.
- **`作废`** — live (waste void), but it means voiding a RECORD, not retrieving
  goods.

**THE CHIP IS REGISTERED IN THE ADMIN DICTIONARY**
(`public/retail-admin/10-extras.js`), which its neighbour is not: `Needs a call`
has had no entry since §98 and has been showing an English chip in a Chinese
admin ever since. Recorded here because it is a live gap somebody should close,
and because not repeating it was a decision rather than an accident.

## Which box has gone (2026-09-19, §190)

§188 told the customer of a parked order that *one of the parcels* had shipped.
On a split order that is two boxes arriving on different days, so the sentence
made them count boxes to work out which one had landed. Ash: *"ok do it"*, on
the flag §188 left.

**Register: CUSTOMER** (Rule 1). **Nothing here is a new word** — every mode
already has a locked pair, and `Air · 空运` / `Land · 陆运` are already
customer-facing on the printed slip (`lib/feie.js`, whose own comment says the
receipt is customer-facing). Only the three sentences are composed, and each is
a live mode word in front of §188's live `包裹已发货`.

| mode | EN | CN | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `air` | the air parcel has shipped | 空运包裹已发货 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — live `空运` + §188's live `包裹已发货` |
| `land` | the land parcel has shipped | 陆运包裹已发货 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — live `陆运` + the same |
| `local` | the same-city parcel has shipped | 同城包裹已发货 | **COMPOSED**, 2026-09-19 — live `同城` (`public/m.html` parcel word) + the same |
| *anything else* | one of the parcels has shipped | 其中一个包裹已发货 | §188, unchanged |

**THE FALLBACK IS NOT DEAD CODE AND IS NOT A GUESS.** A supplier parcel cannot
reach this sentence — the dispatch route refuses those outright — so the branch
exists for a mode added LATER, whose customer word will not exist on the day it
is added. A new mode should read slightly vague rather than wrong, and a
fallback is what stops the next person inventing a pair in a hurry to fill it.

**同城 RATHER THAN 同城配送.** The longer form is live too, in the operator
drawer's mode pill (`Local delivery · 同城配送`), and it is the OPERATOR
register's word for the shipping method. The customer is being told about a box,
not about a method, and `public/m.html` already shortens it to `同城` for exactly
that reading. Rule 1: the cross-register difference is deliberate.

**THE TITLE IS UNCHANGED** — `Part of your order has shipped · 订单部分已发货`.
The mode belongs in the body beside the order number, where the customer is
already reading a specific fact about a specific parcel; a title that varied by
mode would give one notification three shapes in the list.


## A parcel the shortage is holding (2026-09-19, §193)

§187 gave the parked order's healthy box its dispatch button back and refused
the box that carries a short line by name — `parcel_awaiting_restock`. The code
went to the UI and **no pair was registered for it**, so `tdErrorText` fell
through to its last resort and printed *Parcel awaiting restock* in English, in
a Chinese admin, on both routes that raise it. §193 makes the JD waybill route a
third caller and the busiest one, which is what turned a quiet gap into a
sentence somebody reads.

**Register: OPERATOR** (Rule 1). **Nothing here is composed.** Both halves are
live verbatim and the pair is their join.

| EN | CN | source |
|---|---|---|
| That parcel is waiting on a restock. | 该包裹正在等待补货。 | **LIFTED**, 2026-09-19 — `该包裹` from `invalid_shipment_id` in the same dictionary (`该包裹不属于此订单。`); `正在等待补货。` verbatim from `lib/push-events.js` (`顾客已付款，或订单正在等待补货。`) |

**THE SUBJECT IS THE BOX, NOT THE LINE INSIDE IT.** What the server actually
knows is that this parcel holds one or more products the order is parked on —
`parcelHeldLines` counts them. A sentence naming the count was considered and
dropped: the operator has the hold pill on the same screen for that
(`待补货 — N 项`, live since §187), the toast is the refusal and not the report,
and an error string that has to be built from a number is one more place for the
two to disagree about one parcel.

Rejected, and why:

- **`该订单正在等待补货。`** — the order, not the parcel. Live-adjacent and
  wrong in the one way this whole section exists to prevent: §187's rule is that
  a parked ORDER is not a parked BOX, and an error saying *the order* is waiting
  would tell the operator the opposite of what the button beside it does.
- **`该包裹尚不可发货。`** — lifted from `not_shippable`'s live
  `该订单尚不可发货。` by swapping the noun. Readable, and it names the refusal
  without naming the cause, which is the exact complaint that produced §193: the
  operator's next question is *why*, and `待补货` is the word every other
  control on that screen already answers it with.
- **`缺货`** — live in the product-stock sense (*out of stock*). It describes
  the shelf, not this order's wait, and the admin already reserves `待补货` /
  `等待补货` for the wait.

## A pre-order's restock window — the checkout popup (2026-09-20)

Rule 4 is worked in order under the standing delegation of *The delegation
becomes standing*: a live pair first, the source second, composing last. **Every
word below is live**; what is composed is one clause and the join.

### The customer register — what a shopper reads at checkout

| key | EN | CN | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preorderWindow` (range) | `2-4 days` | `2-4 天` | numeral + the live day counter `天`; nothing composed |
| `preorderWindow` (single) | `3 days` / `1 day` | `3 天` | as above; only the EN plural branches |
| `preorderRestockClause` | `they are usually back in stock within {window}` | `预计 {window} 内补货` | **COMPOSED** by Claude (Opus), 2026-09-20 — all three words live |

**THE SENTENCE AROUND IT IS NOT COMPOSED AND IS NOT RETIRED.** The default
message a tenant sees with no window set is the one that has shipped since this
notice existed, character for character:

> 您订单中的部分商品目前缺货。此为预订订单，我们将在补货后尽快为您一并发货。

With a window set, the clause is inserted and nothing else moves:

> 您订单中的部分商品目前缺货。此为预订订单，**预计 2-4 天内补货**，我们将在补货后尽快为您一并发货。

**HOW THE CLAUSE WAS ARRIVED AT, word by word.** `预计` is live and
customer-facing in two places for exactly this sense — an estimate, not a
recorded fact: the order page's `预计送达` and the fresh-batch notice's
`预计 {delivery_date} 新鲜送达`. That matters under Rule 2, which bans a word that
asserts a past event from labelling an estimate; `预计` is the product's own
estimate word and carries the hedge the English "usually" carries. `补货` is live
in the very sentence this clause joins (`我们将在补货后尽快为您一并发货`) and in the
order status `等待补货`, so the clause and its neighbours name the same event with
the same word. `内` is live as the within-a-span particle in `48 小时内` (the
fresh-batch tip) and `30 天内` (the sign-in screen). `天` is the live day counter
throughout.

**TWO CANDIDATES WERE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, recorded so the search is not
repeated.** **`到货`** — live, and the more natural word for goods ARRIVING —
names arrival at the customer's door, which is not what this window measures: the
estimate is when OUR shelf is refilled, and the courier leg is still ahead of it.
Using it would promise a delivery date the system has not computed, which is the
§138 exposure this notice exists inside. **`通常`** ("usually") maps the English
hedge more literally than `预计` does, but it is not live anywhere in this product
and `预计` already carries the hedge in the register a customer meets it in, so
the live pair wins under preference 1.

**REGISTER: CUSTOMER** (Rule 1). The orders-list chip and the order drawer keep
`预订` whatever a tenant writes here, and that is deliberate — see the operator
table below.

### The operator register — the back-office card

Every pair here is admin-facing. Where the Fresh batches card already had a pair
for the same control it is **lifted whole**, so an operator who has configured
one card meets no new vocabulary on the other.

| key | EN | CN | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preorderCard` | `Pre-orders` | `预订` | LIFTED — the notice's own live kicker |
| `preorderPopup` | `Checkout popup` | `结账弹窗` | LIFTED from the Fresh batches card |
| `preorderEyebrow` | `Popup eyebrow` | `弹窗小标题` | LIFTED from the Fresh batches card |
| `preorderTitle` | `Popup title` | `弹窗标题` | LIFTED from the Fresh batches card |
| `preorderNotice` | `Checkout notice` | `结账提示` | LIFTED from the Fresh batches card |
| `preorderWindowField` | `Restock window` | `预计补货时间` | **COMPOSED** by Claude (Opus), 2026-09-20 — `预计` + `补货` + `时间`, all live |
| `preorderWindowFrom` | `From` | `最快(天)` | **COMPOSED** by Claude (Opus), 2026-09-20 |
| `preorderWindowTo` | `To` | `最慢(天)` | **COMPOSED** by Claude (Opus), 2026-09-20 |
| `preorderHubDefault` | `Default wording · no time named` | `默认文案 · 未提时间` | **COMPOSED** by Claude (Opus), 2026-09-20 — `默认文案` lifted from the Fresh batches card's *any field blank* line |
| `preorderHubCustom` | `Own wording` | `自定义文案` | **COMPOSED** by Claude (Opus), 2026-09-20 |
| `preorderHubWindow` | `Back in stock within X` | `预计 X 内补货` | the customer clause above, reused on the hub status line |

**`最快` / `最慢` RATHER THAN `最少` / `最多`.** The boxes hold days of waiting,
and fast/slow is how a wait is described; least/most reads as a quantity of goods,
which is what every other numeric box on these screens holds. Neither pair is
live for this control. **Ash should correct either if it reads wrong to a Chinese
operator; nothing depends on the exact phrasing.**

**THE OPERATOR CHIP DOES NOT FOLLOW THE TENANT'S COPY, and that is Rule 1 rather
than a gap.** A tenant who renames the popup's eyebrow to something seasonal does
not rename the `预订` chip on the orders list or in the order drawer. Cross-register
differences are deliberate: an operator scanning a list needs one stable word for
the state whatever sentence the storefront is currently running.

**`{window}` IS THE ONLY PLACEHOLDER, AND IT CAN BE ABSENT, WHICH NO OTHER
PLACEHOLDER IN THIS PRODUCT CAN.** `{ship_date}`, `{delivery_date}` and
`{make_date}` are computed when their notice fires and always resolve. This one
is typed and can be cleared, so operator copy that asks for a window with no days
behind it falls back to the built-in sentence whole. A half-sentence
(`…内补货` with nothing before it, or the English `within .`) must never reach a
customer, and the failure would be invisible to whoever cleared the boxes.

## One word for a reservable row — the browse band (2026-09-20)

**RETIREMENT, not a composition.** Nothing is minted here. One live pair stops
being drawn in one register and another live pair takes its place there.

| key | EN | CN | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bandReservable` | PRE-ORDER | 可预订 | **LIVE, now on every browse surface** |
| `bandReservable` (PDP buy button) | PRE-ORDER | 预订 | LIVE, unchanged — a button says what it does |
| ~~`bandShipsSoon`~~ | ~~SHIPS SOON~~ | ~~现订现发~~ | **RETIRED FROM THE BAND** — still live as the popup title |

**WHAT WAS WRONG.** The shop grid and the web storefront card drew
`SHIPS SOON · 现订现发`. The PDP badge, the PDP buy button, the PDP size rows,
the shop's variant size sheet and the favourites tile drew `PRE-ORDER · 可预订`.
Same product, same shelf state, two words — and the word changed as the shopper
tapped from the card into the page. Rule 1 calls a within-register difference a
defect, and this was one, five surfaces to two.

**HOW THE SPLIT SURVIVED.** It was written down as a reason rather than as a
defect: the grid's own note argued the website *"names the promise instead of
the mechanism"*. That is a real distinction and it is not being called wrong —
it is being outvoted by the five surfaces that never adopted it. It also fought
the window §195 appends: **`SHIPS SOON · 2-4 DAYS` says soon and then says how
long**, which is the reading the band exists to save a shopper from.

`scripts/test_fresh_today_label.js` had been asserting both halves in a single
case whose NAME read *"a GROCERY row is the carve-out: no batch is being cooked,
so PRE-ORDER stands"* while its second line asserted `SHIPS SOON`. The test knew.

**WHERE THE RETIRED PAIR STAYS, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A HALF-RETIREMENT.**
`现订现发` remains the default TITLE of the checkout pre-order popup
(`computePreorderNotice`). Rule 1's two registers: the band names the STATE a
shopper is browsing, the popup titles the PROMISE at the moment they commit.
Retiring it there was never the change, and a tenant may now rewrite it anyway
(§194).

**`预订` VS `可预订` ON THE PDP BUTTON IS DELIBERATE AND UNCHANGED.** The badge
says what the row IS (`可预订` — reservable); the button says what the tap DOES
(`预订` — reserve). A button that reads "reservable" describes itself instead of
offering an action. Both are live and both predate this entry.

### The window in the band's register

| key | EN | CN | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bandRestockWindow` (range) | `2-4 DAYS` | `2-4 天` | numerals + the live `天`; upper case because the band is |
| `bandRestockWindow` (single) | `3 DAYS` / `1 DAY` | `3 天` | as above; only the EN plural branches |

Drawn as `PRE-ORDER · 2-4 DAYS` / `可预订 · 2-4 天`, on the separator
`withFreshArrival` already uses — a reader comparing two rows must not be able
to tell which appender drew which.

**THE SAME NUMBER APPEARS IN TWO CASES AND THAT IS A REGISTER DIFFERENCE, NOT
DRIFT.** The band is upper case (`2-4 DAYS`); the checkout popup says the same
window lower case inside a sentence (`usually back in stock within 2-4 days`).
Chinese has no case, so both read `2-4 天` and the two must be identical there —
`scripts/test_preorder_band.js` asserts exactly that, and folds the English case
out before comparing the four implementations.

**A ZERO-DAY WINDOW IS NOT DRAWN, IN ANY REGISTER.** `0/0` would read
`PRE-ORDER · 0 DAYS` on the band and *"within 0 days"* in the popup. The first
is §80's defect — a label describing a wait that is not happening — and the
second is not a sentence anyone writes on purpose. Treated as unset everywhere.
A range that merely STARTS at zero (`0-2 天`) is a real window and is kept.

**NOT DRAWN ON THE ADD-TO-ORDER PICKER**, which takes the renamed word and
neither appender. §170 ruled that an add-on picker is not a browse surface and
kept its date off that screen; a window arriving without that date would leave
the list reading `PRE-ORDER · 2-4 DAYS` beside a bare `NEXT BATCH`. Both
appenders arrive together or neither does.

## A product's own notice at the basket (2026-09-20, §197)

A tenant can put a warning on a product — *"this kombucha is alive; stand it in
the fridge overnight before you open it"* — and it is raised when the product
goes into the basket, restated on the product page, and restated again on the
order. Rule 4 worked in order under the standing delegation of *The delegation
becomes standing*.

**NOTHING CUSTOMER-FACING IS COMPOSED HERE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CHARACTER OF
THIS CHANGE.** Every word a shopper reads on the card is the TENANT'S OWN, typed
into the product editor in both languages. The only chrome the card carries of
its own is its button, and that is `知道了` — live on all four checkout notice
cards, the mini app's content-check dialog and the admin keyboard sheet. The
card's badge is `!`, which belongs to no language.

### The operator register — the product editor's card

| key | EN | CN | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| accordion | `Add-to-cart notice` | `加入购物车提示` | **COMPOSED** by Claude (Opus), 2026-09-20 — both halves live |
| picker label | `Notice` | `提示` | live |
| picker, none | `— None` | `无提示` | **COMPOSED** — `无` and `提示` both live |
| picker, new | `+ New notice` | `新建提示` | **COMPOSED** — `新建` and `提示` both live |
| headline fields | `Headline EN` / `Headline CN` | `标题(英文)` / `标题(中文)` | live, lifted whole |
| message fields | `Message EN` / `Message CN` | `文案(英文)` / `文案(中文)` | live, lifted whole |
| bilingual hint | `English · 中文 — customers see one, based on their WeChat language.` | `顾客按微信语言看到其中一种。` | live, lifted whole from the pop-ups editor |
| message placeholder | `One or two short lines.` | `一两句简短文字。` | live, lifted whole from the pop-ups editor |
| headline placeholder | `e.g. Let it rest before you open it` | `例如:开瓶前请先静置` | **COMPOSED** |
| what it does | `Shown once when a customer adds this product to the basket, and again on their order.` | `顾客将本商品加入购物车时显示一次,并在订单页再次显示。` | **COMPOSED** |
| what editing does | `Editing these words changes the notice for every product it is on.` | `修改此处文字会影响所有使用该提示的商品。` | **COMPOSED** |
| save failure | `Notice not saved` | `提示未保存` | **COMPOSED** — `未保存` live |

**HOW `加入购物车提示` WAS ARRIVED AT.** `加入购物车` is the mini app's own button
and toast for this exact gesture — it is what the shopper taps and what the
confirmation says — so the control is named after the thing it fires on, in the
words the product already uses for it. `提示` is the product's noun for a notice
shown to a customer: `结账提示` (checkout notice), `空购物车提示` (empty-basket
notice), `新鲜提示` (freshness tip) are all live admin labels, and the second of
those already contains `购物车提示` as a live construction. The compound is new;
neither half is.

**ONE CANDIDATE WAS REJECTED AND THE REJECTION IS THE POINT.** **`加购提示`** is
shorter and `加购` is live — but live in a DIFFERENT SENSE: `加购获得` on the
loyalty ledger, `下单后又加购了商品` on the orders pill and `下单后加购` on the phone
all mean *added to an order after it was paid for* (§ the add-on flow). A control
named `加购提示` would read to an operator as a notice about ORDER ADD-ONS, which
is a real and different feature in this product. Rule 2's ban on a word that
asserts the wrong event applies to operator labels as much as customer ones, so
the longer, unambiguous compound wins over the live-but-wrong one.

**THE TWO HELPER SENTENCES ARE COMPOSED FROM LIVE PARTS.** `顾客` (522 live),
`本商品` (live in the product editor's own copy), `加入购物车`, `显示`, `订单页`,
`修改`, `文字`, `影响` and `商品` are each live and admin-facing. What is new is
the sentences, because nothing in this product has previously had to say *this is
shown once, at the basket, and shared between products*.

**THE HEADLINE PLACEHOLDER IS COMPOSED and is example text, not a label.** It
exists to show an operator what belongs in the field, and it is deliberately the
case Ash described. `开瓶` (open the bottle) is not otherwise live; `静置` (let it
stand) is not otherwise live. Both are ordinary Chinese for what they say and
neither is a term this product defines elsewhere, so nothing can drift against
them. A tenant who types over it — which is the point of a placeholder — ships
none of it.

**REGISTER: OPERATOR** (Rule 1) for every pair above. The CUSTOMER register for
this feature is the tenant's own text plus `知道了`, and this document locks
neither: a tenant's own words about their own product are theirs.

## The supplier's stock-request slip (§198)

**WHAT THIS IS.** A request raised by one shop against another now prints at the
shop that has to fill it, on that shop's own printer. Everything on the paper is
a string that was already live; the one composed string is in the setting that
switches the paper on, which is an office screen and not the slip.

### On the slip — nothing composed

| Where | English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| slip title | Stock request | 补货申请 | **LOCKED** — the pair `restock:request` carries in `lib/capabilities.js` and the one `申请` in the receipt vocabulary was matched to |
| destination line | For {shop} | 送到 {shop} | **LIFTED** — `public/m.html`'s live `For which store? · 送到哪家门店？`, with the question dropped and the shop's own name supplied |
| item block head | Items 件数 | — | **LIVE** — `lib/feie.js`'s packing slip, verbatim, one glued pair as it already prints there |
| note head | Note 备注 | — | **LIVE** — `lib/feie.js`'s kitchen request, verbatim |
| time | Time | — | **LIVE** — same slip, same line |

**THE SHOP NAMED ON IT IS THE DESTINATION AND THAT IS A VOCABULARY DECISION AS
WELL AS A LAYOUT ONE.** The person holding the slip is standing in the supplying
shop. Printing their own name back at them names where they are; the name worth
ink is the one that decides where the goods go. It is the same rule the `sent`
push already follows — *"which end is worth naming is the end the reader is not
at"*.

**NO PRICE, NO TOTAL, NO COST.** §51 ruled this for the kitchen ticket and the
reason carries unchanged: a transfer moves value between two shelves of one
business, and a money column invites the shop filling it to think the other one
owes them something.

### The setting — one composed sentence

| Where | English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| settings, heading | Stock requests | 补货申请 | **LOCKED**, as above |
| settings, help | A stock request prints at the shop that has to fill it, the moment it is sent. It uses that shop's own printer — the one set below — so there is nothing extra to configure. | 补货申请发出时,在供货门店自动打印,使用该门店下方设置的打印机,无需另行配置。 | **COMPOSED** under Rule 4's standing delegation — see below |
| settings, option | When a request arrives | 请求到达时 | **LIVE PAIR** — the kitchen printer's own `When it prints` select in `public/retail-admin.html`, verbatim |
| settings, option | Never — notification only | 不打印,仅通知 | **LIVE PAIR** — same select, verbatim |

**THE COMPOSED SENTENCE, AND WHAT WAS REJECTED.** The live candidate was §51's
kitchen help — `制作请求进入队列时,厨房自动打印制作单;没有打印机则留空。` — and it
was REJECTED rather than adapted, for a reason worth recording: its last clause
tells the reader to leave the SN blank if there is no printer, and this setting
has no SN to leave blank. It routes on the shop map further down the same page.
A sentence ending in an instruction the screen cannot carry out is worse than no
sentence.

What was kept from it is the SHAPE — *when it happens, then what prints, then
where it is configured* — and every word inside is live: `补货申请` is locked,
`自动打印` and `打印机` are both in that same kitchen help line, `供货门店` is
`供货` joined to the `门店` this document uses throughout, and `无需另行配置` is
the plainest reading of "nothing extra to configure". Composed by Claude Opus 5
on 2026-09-20 under the 2026-09-06 amendment, declared here in the same commit
as the code that uses it.

**`供货` IS THE ONE WORD WORTH FLAGGING FOR A READER WHO SPEAKS THE LANGUAGE.**
It means to supply goods, and it is the right word for the end this slip prints
at, but it does not otherwise appear in this system's vocabulary — every other
screen says `门店` and lets position carry the direction. If Ash prefers the
plainer `发货门店` (the shop that sends), that is a one-word change in
`public/retail-admin.html` and this row.


## The asker's own list (§198)

**WHAT THIS IS.** *Your stock requests* — what became of what you asked another
shop for. It is §175's screen written for the other request, and its vocabulary
is that screen's wherever the two say the same thing, which is nearly
everywhere.

**THE TWO SCREENS MUST NOT DRIFT APART, and that is a vocabulary rule and not
only a design one.** They sit under one heading on one phone, four rows apart.
A reader who learns `待处理` on one and meets a different word for the same
state on the other has been taught that the two are different things.

### Composed — two, each one noun away from a live pair

| Where | English | Chinese | Built from |
|---|---|---|---|
| the More row, and the screen title | Your stock requests | 我的补货申请 | **COMPOSED** — `Your buying requests · 我的采购申请` is live in `public/m.html`, and `采购` is swapped for the locked `补货`. Both halves of the result are live: `我的…申请` is the sibling row's own shape and `补货申请` is locked. |
| empty state, second line | What you ask another shop for shows up here, and what became of it. | 你向其他门店提交的补货申请及其进展会显示在这里。 | **COMPOSED** — the sibling's live `你向采购提交的申请及其进展会显示在这里。` with its one wrong noun replaced: `采购` (the buyer) becomes `其他门店` (another shop), and the bare `申请` becomes the locked `补货申请` because with the buyer gone the word alone no longer says which kind. Sentence shape, punctuation and ending are that pair's, untouched. |

Composed by Claude Opus 5 on 2026-09-20 under the 2026-09-06 amendment, declared
here in the same commit as the code that uses them.

**WHAT WAS REJECTED.** `调拨` — transfer — was the obvious alternative for the
title and is live in this system (`调拨收货`, and the refusal `这是门店之间的调拨`).
It was rejected because **the screen is not about transfers, it is about
ASKING**: it lists things nobody has agreed to send yet, and half of what it
shows will read `待处理` forever if the supplier never picks it. `补货申请` says
what the row on it actually is. The word `调拨` remains correct on the two
screens that handle goods genuinely in motion, and is deliberately left there.

### Lifted whole — nothing composed

| Where | English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty state, first line | Nothing asked for yet | 还没有申请 | **LIVE PAIR** — the Ask-to-buy companion, `public/m.html`, verbatim |
| read failed | That list could not be read. Try again. | 无法读取列表，请重试。 | **LIVE PAIR** — same screen, verbatim, and it exists for the same reason: an empty list and a list that could not be read are different things |
| line state | Waiting | 待处理 | **LIVE PAIR** — same screen's `mbsWord`, verbatim; the same word for the same state on both |
| line state | Dispatched | 已发货 | **LIVE** — `public/m.html`, the parcel's own word (`包裹已发货`), with the noun the screen already supplies dropped |
| line state | Counted in | 已点收 | **LIVE PAIR** — `routes/restock.js`'s own `received` notification title, verbatim. The screen and the push that announces the same event now say the same word, which they did not before only because the screen did not exist. |
| quantity actually sent | {n} sent | {n} 已发出 | **LIVE** — `已发出` is live across `public/m.html` and the desktop admin; the numeral is a numeral |
| header, withdrawn | Withdrawn | 已撤回 | **LIVE PAIR** — the Ask-to-buy companion, verbatim |

**THE SHOP'S NAME IS NOT A STRING.** The header names the shop the request was
asked of, and it is that shop's own `name_cn` / `name_en` read off its row —
typed by whoever set the shop up, never translated here and never composed. A
name is not vocabulary.


## Somebody is waiting on you (§198)

**WHAT THIS IS.** Two toasts, announcing that another shop has asked this one
for stock. They ride the Pick row's dot — the row had no mark of any kind, so a
push was the only thing that ever said a request had arrived, and a push is one
moment on one phone that may be in a pocket.

**THE DOT ITSELF HAS NO STRING**, which is the first thing to say about it. It
is a 6px Sage dot and never a number: a count in the chrome turns arriving work
into an alarm, and the number belongs on the screen it points at. That rule is
already written on the tab bar's dots and is only being obeyed here.

| Where | English | Chinese | Built from |
|---|---|---|---|
| toast, one | A shop has asked you for stock | 有门店向你发起补货申请 | **COMPOSED** — `发起补货申请` is VERBATIM the label `lib/capabilities.js` gives `restock:request`, the capability this very row is gated on; `有门店` is live in `public/m.html` (four places); `向你` is the plainest join. |
| toast, several | {n} shops are waiting on you | {n} 家门店正在等待发货 | **COMPOSED** — `正在等待` is lifted from `lib/push-events.js`'s live `正在等待补货。`, with its noun swapped for `发货`, which is live across this file and the desktop admin. `家…门店` is the ordinary measure for shops and `{n}` is a numeral. |

Composed by Claude Opus 5 on 2026-09-20 under the 2026-09-06 amendment,
declared here in the same commit as the code that uses them.

**WHY THE SINGULAR AND THE PLURAL ARE DIFFERENT SENTENCES rather than one with a
number in it.** The Chinese is the reason. `1 家门店正在等待发货` is not wrong,
but it reads as a report on a queue; the thing that has actually happened when
the count goes from nothing to one is that a shop has ASKED, and the word for
asking is the one the capability already uses. The kitchen's own arrival toast
splits the same way and for the same reason, and the two now match.

**NO CHIME, AND NO RED.** A chime belongs to a customer arriving; this is a
colleague asking. The pill and the dot spend Sage, never Brick — an arriving
request is work, not a fault, and `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` has said
what Brick is reserved for since it was first spent.

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SAID.** The toast names no shop and no product. It
fires from a count, and a count cannot honestly name anything; the screen one
tap away names both. A toast that guessed which shop would be wrong the first
time two asked at once.


## An order that never left the shelf (§200)

**WHAT THIS NAMES.** A transfer whose paperwork says sent and whose stock never
moved. It had no screen at all until §200's amendment — it is off the Pick run
and off the Receive list — so it had never needed words, and the words it
needs are unusually load-bearing: the person reading them has to understand
that the SYSTEM is wrong, not them.

| Where | English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| band heading | Did not leave the shelf | 未实际发货 | **COMPOSED** — `实际` and `发货` are both live throughout `public/m.html`; the negation is the plainest form. Says what did not happen, not who failed to do it. |
| band body | Marked sent, but the stock never moved, so the shop cannot count it in. | 已标记发出,但库存未实际扣减,门店无法点收。 | **COMPOSED** from live words only: `已标记` (7 live uses), `扣减` (8), `库存`, `门店` and `点收` — the last verbatim from `routes/restock.js`'s own `已点收` notification, so the band and the alert that closes the loop use one word. |
| the button | Send again | 重新发货 | **LIFTED** — `重新打印` is live in `public/retail-admin/04-orders.js` (§51 registered it); `重新` carries, and `发货` is the verb this screen does instead of printing. |
| the button, busy | Sending… | 发送中… | **LIVE PAIR** — `public/m.html`'s own `打印中…` shape with its live verb `发送`; the ellipsis is that pair's. |
| toast, moved | Sent — the shop can count it in now | 已发出 — 门店可以点收了 | **COMPOSED** — `已发出` and `点收` both live, joined by the em dash this file's toasts already use. |
| toast, already gone | Those goods had already left | 这批货此前已发出 | **COMPOSED** — `此前` (2 live uses) and `已发出`; it answers the second tap, and must read as reassurance rather than a refusal, because tapping twice is the ordinary thing a person does when they are not sure the first one worked. |

Composed by Claude Opus 5 on 2026-09-20 under the 2026-09-06 amendment,
declared here in the same commit as the code that uses them.

**IT SAYS WHAT DID NOT HAPPEN, NEVER WHO DID NOT DO IT.** The picker did press
Send; the system took the press and moved nothing. Wording that read as *"you
did not send this"* would be false as well as unkind, and the English was
written first with that constraint and the Chinese built to match it.

**AMBER, NOT BRICK, AND THAT IS A VOCABULARY DECISION TOO.** Brick is reserved
for a fault; this is work still owed. The colour and the words have to agree,
or one of them is lying.


## The four words a line can wear (§202)

**WHAT CHANGED AND WHY IT IS A VOCABULARY MATTER.** *Your stock requests* had
three states and the middle one, *Dispatched*, was lit by the picker's tick.
Ticking happens at the shelf; dispatching happens when the van leaves. One word
covered both and was wrong about one of them, which sent Ash to a screen that
correctly said the opposite.

| State | English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| nobody has touched it | Waiting | 待处理 | **LIVE PAIR** — this screen's own, and the Ask-to-buy companion's before it |
| ticked at the supplier | Picked | 已拣 | **LIFTED VERBATIM** from the Pick screen's counter, `n/n 已拣` — the screen where the tick is made |
| the run has left | On its way | 在途 | **LIVE** — the half of `On the way` in this file's order filters (`在途 / 待发送`) |
| counted in at the far end | Counted in | 已点收 | **LIVE PAIR** — `routes/restock.js`'s own `received` notification |

**`已拣` IS THE ONE WORTH EXPLAINING.** It is taken from the Pick screen rather
than composed for this one, and deliberately: the person who makes the tick and
the person who asked for the goods now read **the same word for the same act**.
A separate word would have been two names for one event, which is how two
screens come to disagree — the very fault this section exists to fix.

**WHAT WAS REJECTED.** `已发货` — the old middle word, live and correct
elsewhere — is not reused for *Picked*, because it says the goods have GONE and
at that moment they have not. It keeps its job on the parcel screens, where it
is true.

**NOTHING IS COMPOSED, AND THE GATE IS NOW STRUCTURAL.**
`scripts/test_stock_request_mine.js` counts each Chinese half across `public/`
and `routes/` and requires at least two uses, so a word minted for this screen
fails rather than shipping quietly. That is the first time this document's rule
is enforced by a suite instead of by a reader remembering it.

**ONLY THE LAST STATE SPENDS A COLOUR.** Sage on *Counted in*; the two middle
states are neutral. Arriving is the end of the journey — the others are
progress, and progress that shouts stops being read.


## Four ways to say no rider yet (§203)

**WHAT THIS NAMES.** The line in the order drawer's *Same-city courier* block
when no delivery exists on the courier platform yet. There are four reasons for
that and the block had three sentences, because the two most different reasons
shared one:

| Row state | What is true | What it said before |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` / `processing` | nobody has drained it yet | Queued for push… |
| `ready` | **checked, and deliberately held until staff call the delivery** | Queued for push… |
| held on a geocoder outage | the map service is down, it retries itself | Held — map service unavailable |
| `error` / `skipped` | refused; a person must act | Push refused |

The second row is the healthy resting state of every booked order. Saying it
with the first row's words told a store that an order working exactly as
designed was an order nothing had looked at.

| Where | English | Chinese | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| the line, booked | No courier called yet | 尚未呼叫运力 | **LIFTED VERBATIM** — the ship-from confirm body in `public/retail-admin/04-orders.js` has said `尚未呼叫运力,不产生费用` since the override shipped. Same drawer, same fact, so it is the same words. |
| the note, booked | The address is checked. Compare couriers below when you want a rider — nothing is charged until you dispatch. | 地址已核对。需要骑手时点击下方“查看运力比价” — 发起配送前不产生费用。 | **COMPOSED from live fragments only**: `已核对` (5 live uses, incl. `付款已核对` on this screen), `查看运力比价` **verbatim from the button it points at**, `骑手` (79 live uses), `不产生费用` from the same confirm body as the line above. No new character. |
| the line, waiting | Queued for push… · 4m ago | 排队发单中… · 4 分钟前 | **UNCHANGED PAIR plus `courierAgo`'s own** — the age is rendered by the drawer's existing ago-helper, whose `分钟前` is live throughout this file. |

Composed by Claude Opus 5 on 2026-09-21 under the 2026-09-06 amendment,
declared here in the same commit as the code that uses it.

**THE NOTE NAMES THE BUTTON THAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE SCREEN.** `查看运力比价` is
not a description of the action, it is the label of the control three lines
below it, quoted. A note that said *"compare the couriers"* in any other words
would be a second name for one button, which is how a screen comes to disagree
with itself — the same reasoning §202 gives for taking `已拣` from the Pick
screen rather than minting one.

**WHAT WAS REJECTED.** `待呼叫` — tidy, and the obvious mint for "waiting to be
called" — is not used. It is not live anywhere in this system, and the live
phrase already says the same thing in words a picker has read before. `已就绪` /
*Ready* was rejected for a different reason: it is the queue row's internal
status name, and naming a screen after a database enum teaches the reader the
schema instead of the situation.

**THE AGE IS NOT DECORATION.** Two minutes of `排队发单中…` is the geocoder
working; two hours is a stall, and before this both printed the identical five
words. The age is spent only on the plain wait — the hold carries `自 HH:MM`
already, the booked state is not waiting on us, and a refusal is not a wait at
all.

**NO COLOUR IS SPENT ON THE BOOKED STATE.** Amber is for the hold and the
refusal, which are things going wrong. A booked order waiting for someone to
call a rider is ordinary work, and ordinary work that shouts stops being read.
Its tick is the same neutral grey as the queue wait it replaced.


## The product page's sections and the card that orders them (§206)

**WHAT THIS NAMES.** The full product page (Ash, 2026-09-21: *"build a from
scratch … exactly like the mock up"*) is a rail of six sections, one open at a
time, and a right column that never moves; Settings › Operations › Product page
lets a business order and hide those sections once. **Register: OPERATOR**
(Rule 1) throughout — nothing here is customer-facing.

**COPIED, NOT COMPOSED.** The rail and the section headings are the dock's own
tab strip and card headings, lifted whole: `Basics · 基础`, `Where it shows ·
分类与陈列`, `Cost & Pricing · 成本与定价`, `Stock · 库存`, `How it's sold · 售卖方式`,
`Shopper page · 顾客页面` (the dock's summary row, `09-products.js`). The right
column keeps `Sales · 销量`, `Shipping · 配送方式`, `Free of · 不含`, `Flags · 标记`,
`Internal notes · 内部备注`. The summary rows reuse `Description · 描述`, `Product

## The stage for a rider who is gone (§219)

**Two strings composed, by Claude, 2026-09-22.** Both are assembled from fragments that are live elsewhere in this same drawer; neither introduces a character that was not already shipping.

| slot | shipped | built from |
|---|---|---|
| stage label | `Rider cancelled · 骑手已取消` | the live stale line `状态未更新 — 骑手可能已取消，请核实或另叫一位。`, with `可能` (may) dropped — that word is the hedge, and this stage exists precisely because the hedge is no longer needed |
| card body | `No rider is on this order. Call another courier if it still needs to go. · 此订单目前无人接单。如仍需配送，请另叫一位。` | `此订单无人接单` from the live *Delivery date passed* copy (`此订单无人接单，<date> 已过。`) and `请另叫一位` from the live stale line above |

**Live candidates rejected, and why.**

- `已取消 (Cancelled)` — live in eight places (order status, refund state, purchase orders, JD pickup). **Rejected: it names the wrong noun.** On this card `已取消` alone would read as *the order* is cancelled, which is the one thing that has not happened — the order is still live and still owed to the customer. The subject has to be the rider.
- `骑手可能已取消 (the rider may have cancelled)` — live, and the exact sentence this stage replaces. **Rejected as the label**: it is a guess, and the whole point of the stage is that the guess has been resolved. It stays in the file, unchanged, for the ten minutes before the grace window closes, which is still the only thing we have.
- `再叫一家运力 (Call another courier)` — live on the dispatch button, and **kept**: the body names the action in words the button already uses, so the sentence and the control agree.
- `无骑手 (no rider)` — considered for the body and **rejected as an invention**: nothing in the tree carries it. `无人接单` is live and says the same thing in words the operator has already read on the expired-date surface.

**A numeral needed no label, and that was a correction.** The card's third line is the cancel time rendered by the existing `courierAgo`. It was first written as `Cancelled · 取消于 <ago>`, matching the live `Updated · 更新于 <ago>` a few lines below it — **but `取消于` is live nowhere in the tree**, so that label would have been a third composed string minted to say something the line above already says. It is dropped: the time prints bare, under `Rider cancelled · 骑手已取消`, and reads as the cancel's own clock. Two composed strings, not three.

## Three answers from the reschedule button (§220)

**Two strings composed, by Claude, 2026-09-22.** The existing success wording is unchanged and keeps its meaning; what is new is the two outcomes it used to be printed over.

| outcome | shipped | built from |
|---|---|---|
| a live courier has it | `A courier is already on this one — cancel it in the Qingyun app first · 已呼叫运力。请先在青云 App 取消该单。` | the ship-from line's live pair `A courier is already on this one. To collect it somewhere else, cancel it in the Qingyun app first. · 已呼叫运力。如需改到其他门店取货，请先在青云 App 取消该单。`, with only its middle clause (about collecting somewhere else) dropped — both remaining halves are verbatim |
| the date moved, the queue did not take it | `Moved to today, but it was not re-queued — check the courier · 已改期至今天，但未重新排队 — 请核实运力。` | `已改期至今天` verbatim from the success toast beside it, and `请核实` from the live courier-card line `状态未更新 — 骑手可能已取消，请核实或另叫一位。` |

**Why the second one names both halves.** The customer HAS been told the new day by the time this can happen, so it is not a no-op to press again; and no rider is queued, which is the part still owed. A sentence that said only one of those would send the operator to the wrong next action either way.

**Live candidates rejected.**

- `改期失败 (Could not move it)` — live, the endpoint's own failure toast. **Rejected for both**: nothing failed in either case. The first is a correct refusal and the second is a partial success, and calling either a failure invites a retry that cannot help.
- `已改期至今天 — 已重新排队` — the success pair, and the string the whole change exists to stop over-printing. Kept exactly as it is, now reachable only when the queue actually took the row.

|---|---|---|
| the control | `Change delivery day · 更改配送日期` | `更改` (81 live uses) and `配送日期`, live in the expired surface's own `配送日期已过` |
| the picker's hint | `The rider is called on the morning of the day you pick. Nothing is dispatched before then. · 所选日期当天才会呼叫骑手，在此之前不会发单。` | `当天` (18), `呼叫` (11, incl. the live `已呼叫运力`), `骑手` and `发单` (18, incl. the live `重新发单`) |
| moved to a later day | `Moved to ${date} — the rider is called that morning · 已改期至 ${date} — 当天呼叫骑手` | the live success pair `已改期至今天 — 已重新排队`, with `今天` replaced by the chosen day and the trailing clause rebuilt from the fragments above |

**Why the trailing clause had to change rather than the date alone.** The live pair ends `已重新排队` — *it has gone back in the queue*, which is what an operator is waiting to read and is true for today. For a later day it is a half-truth wearing a tick: the row IS queued and nobody is dispatched for days. Saying "re-queued" over a delivery that will not move until Friday is the same over-promise §219 spent a whole change unpicking, so the day's own sentence says when the rider is called.

**Today keeps its original wording, unchanged.** Two sentences for two genuinely different facts, not one hedged sentence covering both.

**Live candidates rejected.**

- `改期配送 (Reschedule delivery)` — live, the expired surface's own button. **Rejected for the new control**: that button appears after the day has gone and means *put this back in the queue*. This one appears on a live order and means *pick a different day*, which is a choice rather than a recovery. `更改配送日期` says which.
- `已重新排队 (re-queued)` — live, and kept for today. Rejected for a later day, above.
- `等待配送 (Delivery scheduled)` — live, the customer-facing `scheduled` stage. **Rejected**: it is the shopper's word for their own order's state, not an answer to an operator who has just pressed a button, and reusing it here would make the toast read like a status rather than a confirmation.

**The partial-outcome toast was not re-composed.** §219's `已改期至今天，但未重新排队 — 请核实运力。` keeps its frame; `今天` became the chosen day. Same string, different data.

## What Approve will do (§222)

**Five strings composed, by Claude, 2026-09-22.** More than any change should mint, and the reason is worth stating rather than apologising for: **every delivery pair in this file reports something that HAS happened** — 已送达, 已取消, 已改期至今天, 骑手前往取货. Nothing in the tree describes what a button is ABOUT to do, so there was no live sentence of that shape to copy. The nouns and verbs are all live; the sentences are not.

| slot | shipped |
|---|---|
| subtitle | `Lock in the amount. What each mode does is spelled out above the button. · 确认退款金额。各模式的具体影响见按钮上方说明。` |
| full refund | `Full refund: the order is marked refunded, its same-city delivery is cancelled, and stock, points and referral credit are reversed. The customer is told. · 全额退款：订单将标记为已退款，同城配送将被取消，库存、积分与推荐奖励一并退回。系统会通知顾客。` |
| partial refund | `Partial refund: the order keeps its status and its delivery. Stock reverses for the selected items only. The customer is told. · 部分退款：订单状态与配送均不变，仅退回所选商品的库存。系统会通知顾客。` |
| a rider is on it | `A rider is on this order right now — approving cancels that delivery. · 当前已有骑手接单 — 批准后该配送会被取消。` |
| the day is not the money | `Refunding never changes the delivery day. If the customer only wants it another day, reject this and change the date instead. · 退款不会更改配送日期。如顾客只是想改天收货，请拒绝此申请并改期。` |

**Every term inside them is live**: `已退款`, `同城配送`, `库存`, `积分`, `顾客`, `骑手`, `配送日期`, `改期`, `部分退款`, `全额` (from the dialog's own mode labels 全额 / 部分金额 / 按商品). What was assembled is the sentences.

**Live candidates rejected.**

- The old subtitle, `Lock in the amount. Full = order.status flips to refunded + inventory + points reverse…` — English-only, in the language of the columns it writes, and **incomplete**: it never mentioned the courier, which is the one consequence an operator cannot undo. Replaced rather than extended.
- `已取消 (Cancelled)` on its own for the courier clause — **rejected for the same reason as §218**: on a refund dialog it would read as the ORDER being cancelled, which is a different and larger claim than the delivery being pulled. `同城配送将被取消` names what is actually cancelled.
- `确定要退款吗？ (Are you sure?)` — the shape a confirm usually takes here. **Rejected outright**: a question adds a tap and tells the operator nothing they did not already know. The point is not to ask again, it is to say what will happen.

**The last line is the one the change exists for.** A customer with no other way to ask for a different delivery day files a refund asking for one (live order TC000823, 2026-09-22: *"I wnat to get it tomorrow"*), and the button that reads like agreement spends money while moving the date by nothing. It shows in every mode, because the mode is not what makes it true.

## Moved, but the old order may still be live (§223)

**One string composed, by Claude, 2026-09-22.** Every fragment is live and the day is data.

| shipped | built from |
|---|---|
| `Moved to ${day}. The old courier order may still be live — cancel it in the Qingyun app, then call another courier. · 已改期至${day}。运单可能仍在，请先在青云 App 取消该单，再叫一家运力。` | `已改期至` from §220's success toast; `可能` from the live stale warning `骑手可能已取消`; `运单` from `运单号`; `请先在青云 App 取消该单` verbatim from the ship-from lock; `再叫一家运力` verbatim from the dispatch button |

**It is styled as a SUCCESS, which is the decision worth recording.** The operator asked for the day to move and the day moved. What did not happen — a new rider — did not happen on purpose, and the sentence says what finishes it. Dressing that as an error would teach people to distrust a control that did its job.

**Live candidates rejected.**

- `已呼叫运力。请先在青云 App 取消该单。` (§220's live-copy refusal) — **rejected**: it is a refusal, and this is not one. Reusing it would say the move failed when the move succeeded.
- `但未重新排队 — 请核实运力。` (§220's partial outcome) — **rejected**: that sentence is for a queue write that LOST a race and needs checking. Here nothing was attempted, deliberately, and the operator needs an instruction rather than a check.

## Any number of usage tiles (§231)

**One string composed, by Claude, 2026-09-22.** Both words are live; the pair is
not, and the rest of the line is arithmetic.

| shipped | built from |
|---|---|
| `Any number of tiles — the rows even themselves out and the last one always fills (4 → 2+2, 5 → 3+2, 9 → 3+3+3). Each tile: emoji + caps label + optional italic sub-line. · 任意数量 — 4 → 2+2,5 → 3+2,9 → 3+3+3。` | `任意` from `任意订单立减`, `任意评分`, `任意字段留空则使用默认文案。` and a dozen more; `数量` from `低库存提醒数量`, `会员数量`, `预订可售数量`. The examples are numerals and need no words. |

**The Chinese is SHORTER than the English on purpose, and it was already.** The
line it replaces — `6 块 (3 列) 或 8 块 (4 列)。` — did not translate the
sentence about what a tile contains either. This is an editor helper under a
field the office is already looking at, not a customer-facing sentence, and the
numerals carry the whole rule.

**Live candidates rejected.**

- `任意` alone, with the counts doing the rest — **rejected**: on a field that
  takes a LIST, `任意` unqualified reads as *any one of them*, which is the
  opposite instruction. `数量` is what makes it about how many.
- `不限` (live in the delivery rules as *no limit*) — **rejected**: it describes
  a cap that was lifted. Nothing here was ever capped; six and eight were a
  recommendation the grid could not keep.

**Two strings composed, by Claude, 2026-09-23, under the 2026-09-06 amendment.**

| `(shared facility) · （共用生产环境）` (closes the may-contain line) | **composed.** `共用` is live as *shared* (`与其他规格共用`, the variant photo notes in `09-products.js`); `生产环境` is lifted from a live allergen card, Buckwheat Bread's `大豆（生产环境）` over *soy (manufacturing environment)* |

## The proxy watchdog's pages (§263)

**Composed by Claude, 2026-09-25, under the 2026-09-06 amendment.** Register:
OPERATOR (Rule 1): these go to the WeCom proxy alert group, where the owner and
whoever looks after the shop's internet read them. Built in `pageText` in
`lib/proxy-manager.js`; `{…}` are the live path and channel labels
(`门店住宅代理`, `GZ 机房代理`, `直连(香港)`, `天河 外卖`, `越秀 闪购`).

| shipped | built from |
|---|---|
| `🟢 {channel}：{path} 恢复可用` / `{channel}: {path} can reach Meituan again. Nothing to do.` | **copied whole**: the watchdog's own UP page, which it sent on every flap. Now sent only to close a page below |
| `🟠 {channel}：{path}已超过30分钟不可达，当前走 {backup}。请检查门店网络。` / `{channel}: {path} has not reached Meituan for over 30 min. Selling carries on through {backup}. Please check the shop's internet.` | **built from live pieces**: `不可达` and `当前走` are the watchdog's own; `已超过30分钟` is eleme-daemon's order alert (`订单已超过30分钟读取失败`); `门店网络` is the box-setup screen's (`请接入门店网络`); `请检查` is the daemons' own alert shape. The minutes follow `PROXY_DEGRADED_PAGE_MS`. **Composed**: only the order of those pieces |
| `🔴 {channel}：切换到 {direct}，{paths} 均不可达。销售照常，但美团更可能要求验证。请检查门店网络。` / `{channel} is now on {direct}: {paths} cannot reach Meituan. Selling carries on, but Meituan is more likely to ask for a verification check. Please check the shop's internet.` | `切换到` is the watchdog's own; the path list joins live labels with the live `、`. **Composed**: `均` (*all of them*), and `销售照常，但美团更可能要求验证` — `照常` is live (`店面照常运行`), `验证` is live in `验证中心`, which is the challenge this sentence warns of |

**Retired, not reused**: `🟠 {channel}：{path} 不可达` (*another route is being
used instead — nothing to do*), `🔀 {channel}：切换到 {path}` (*switched itself…
nothing to do*), `⚠️ {channel}：启动时已降级，当前走 {path}` (*started up on a
backup route*). Their pieces live on inside the pages above.

**Live candidates rejected.**

- `线路` for *route*: **rejected**, not live anywhere. The page names the paths
  by their live labels instead, which also tells the reader which ones failed.
- `代理掉线` (the daemons' *proxy down, sync paused*): **rejected**. It means
  sync has stopped; these pages go out while selling carries on, and borrowing
  the words would make the two sound equally urgent.
- `订单已超过30分钟读取失败` whole: **rejected**. It is about orders; only its
  `已超过30分钟` is lifted.

write-off's cost (desktop and phone waste screens).

English rewritten to say what the Chinese says; *packed separately* is dropped from both. **Superseded, kept for the record:** `Packed separately — kept if it expires or spoils · 单独包装 — 过期或变质时保留`, composed by Claude 2026-09-27.
| `Not counted as waste: · 不计损耗：` + the line's name | **trimmed from Ash's tick string** (v1.201): `不计损耗` is its last four characters, nothing added. **Superseded, kept for the record:** `Kept, not counted: · 保留，不计入：`, composed by Claude 2026-09-27.

The Chinese N is the whole count, the English N the rest. |
| Every line here is packaging. Nothing is recorded as the contents, so this product has no cost yet. Add what goes inside and the margin appears. | 这里每一行都是包装,没有记录内容,因此本产品暂无成本。添加内容后即显示毛利。 | the figures, a list of packaging only | **composed.** The English is the desktop's (`CN PENDING`). `包装`, `暂无成本` and `毛利` are live, and `内容` is live (`这里没有内容`). |
| “X” needs a quantity greater than zero. | “X”的数量必须大于 0。 | Save, a line at zero | **composed.** The English is the desktop's and the server's (`CN PENDING`). The Chinese is the live `数量必须大于 0。` with the line named. |
| from the product’s net weight (…) | 取自产品净重(…) | a first contents line's quantity | **composed.** The English is the desktop's (`CN PENDING`). `净重` is live (`规格选择器上显示的规格 / 净重`), and the full-width brackets are the house's. |

### Live candidates considered and rejected

- **`物料清单`** for the list itself. Rejected, as `21-product-build.js` asks:
  the labels were arranged so that no name is needed.
- **`无法换算`** anywhere near the unit-cost sentences. Rejected for the reason
  the unit-mismatch lock gives. This is a different fact (no unit cost), and
  it must not borrow that wording.
- **`暂无成本`** for *has no unit cost*. Rejected: that pair means the whole
  thing has no cost yet, and the sentence is about one material's per-unit
  figure. `单位成本` names the figure.
- **`重量`** for *net weight*. Rejected in favour of `净重`, the word the size
  field's own hint uses for the same text.
- **`食谱`** in the copied link strings. Not used: the product editor writes
  配方 throughout, and those pairs are copied as they are. The recipe-search
  failure is the phone's own live `无法加载食谱。`, which is the one place the
  two words meet on this screen.

## A save someone else got to first, on the phone (§337)

**One pair composed, by Claude, 2026-10-01, under the standing delegation (Rule 4 as amended).**
Operator register only (Rule 1): `public/m.html`, `staleSaveText()`. It is shown in two places:
- the category banner card, when the tree save is refused as `stale_tree`;
- the Pop-ups screen, when the switch is refused as `stale_config`.

In both cases the screen has already reloaded what the server holds, so the sentence has to say
that, and no live pair does.

| shipped | built from |
|---|---|
| `Somebody else changed this while you had it open. It has been reloaded — try again.` · `该记录已被他人修改,现已刷新,请重试。` | `01-core.js`'s `row_moved` / `not_mapped` / `not_syncing` refusal, `Somebody else changed this while you had it open — reload and try again. · 该记录已被他人修改,请刷新后重试。`, which the phone already shows for Channel sync (`csErrText`). The first clause is copied whole in both languages. `已刷新` is the desktop's own (`12-guanyi.js`, `Guanyi product list refreshed · 已刷新`). `现` marks it as done rather than asked for. `请重试` is the live pair's own ending without `刷新后`, because the reload has already happened. The comma is the live pair's ASCII `,`. |

**Live candidates rejected:**
- The live pair itself, `…— reload and try again. · …请刷新后重试。`. It tells the operator to reload, but the screen has already done that. On the pop-up switch, a reload by hand would be a second trip for a list that is already on screen.
- `That did not save. Nothing has changed — try again. · 没有保存成功。数据没有变化 — 请重试。` (the pop-up switch's own failure line, still used for every other failure). It says nothing changed. Here something did change: somebody else's edit, which is why the list on screen is now different.
- `This order has already moved on. Close and open it again to see where it is now. · 这个订单已经进入下一步。请关闭后重新打开查看当前状态。`. It is about an order's status.

**Copied whole, unchanged:** `Save failed · 保存失败`, `Saved · 已保存`, `Pop-up is on · 弹窗已启用`,
`Pop-up is off · 弹窗已停用`.

## Ground on an air parcel's label, and the question it asks (§381)

**Operator register (Rule 1), 2026-10-01.** The JD label dialog
(`createJdLabel`, `public/retail-admin/04-orders.js`). An air parcel now lists
the two ground services after air, and picking one asks first. This mirrors
*Air on a land parcel's label, marked rather than hidden (2026-09-16)* above.
The rows themselves are the `JD_SERVICES` labels, unchanged. Nothing new is on
them.

### Reused verbatim

| Chinese | English | Lifted from |
|---|---|---|
| `空运包裹` | Air parcel | this dialog's own subtitle (`空运包裹 — 生鲜特快`), and the parcel card's mode label. Now the question's title |
| `暂不` | Not yet | the land→air question's decline, itself from `transition()` |
| `此包裹` | This parcel | the land→air question's fallback body, `此包裹仅陆运。…` |

### Composed — declared, by Claude, under Rule 4's 2026-09-06 delegation

| Chinese | English | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| `<names> 计划空运,陆运较慢。仍要生成陆运运单吗?` | `<names> — planned for air. Ground is slower. Create the ground waybill anyway?` | The question's body when the parcel's items are known. **Lifted parts:** the item names in bold are the land→air question's own. `计划` + a plan is live in this file: `此订单计划于 <b>…</b> 当天新鲜制作,…` (the early-dispatch question). `空运` and `陆运` are the locked mode words. `仍要生成…运单吗?` is the locked `仍要生成空运运单吗?` with `空运` swapped for `陆运`. **Composed:** `较慢` (slower) — no live Chinese says one service is slower than another, and the question needs to give the reason for asking. **Rejected:** `改走陆运` / `走陆运` — not found anywhere in `public/`, and `生成陆运运单` keeps the parallel with the live air question exactly. **Rejected:** naming 生鲜 spoilage — the parcel may hold nothing fresh (the screenshot's was dates and chips), and a reason that is sometimes false teaches people to skip it |
| `此包裹计划空运,陆运较慢。仍要生成陆运运单吗?` | `This parcel is planned for air. Ground is slower. Create the ground waybill anyway?` | The same body when the order's items are not loaded. `此包裹` opens it, as the land→air fallback does |
| `仍要生成陆运运单` | Create ground waybill anyway | The confirm button. It is the body question without `吗?`, the same pairing as `仍要生成空运运单` / `仍要生成空运运单吗?` |

**English "ground", Chinese 陆运.** The rows say `Fresh · Ground · 生鲜 · 陆运`.
The question uses the same pair as the row being picked, so the two read alike.

**On the phone (2026-10-01, nothing composed).** The phone's JD label sheet (`jdSvc`, `public/m.html`)
asks the same question with every string copied whole from the desktop:
`空运包裹`, both bodies, `仍要生成陆运运单` and `暂不`. Nothing new was composed.
`scripts/test_mobile_jd_waybill.js` fails if the phone's words drift from the
desktop's.

## The switches that stop orders everywhere, on the phone (§390)

**Operator register (Rule 1), 2026-10-01.** The Sales screen, its channel sheet
and the Meituan and Eleme screens (`public/m.html`). The labels are copied from
the desktop's open/close panel (`public/retail-admin/02-settings-ops.js`, its
heading in `retail-admin.html`), the Sales card toggle (`01-core.js`
csChannelToggle) and the channel switches (`11-meituan.js`, `14-eleme.js`).

The desktop asks no question before most of these. Where it does, it gives a
title and nothing else. So the confirm bodies are composed. Each one says what
the server does, read from the handlers, and is built from the phone's live
per-store and per-shop confirms next to it.

| `The mini app and web store stop taking new orders, and shoppers there see that the store is closed. | `The mini app and web store take new orders again, wherever their own channel is open. · 小程序与网店将在各自渠道开启的门店恢复接新订单。` | **composed by Claude.** It says the switch does not override a channel closed on its own card. |
| `Close everything? · 全部关闭？` / `Open everything? · 全部营业？` | **restructured.** The desktop's live button pairs, with a question mark added. `全部关闭` is copied whole from the desktop's master button. v1.137 rejected it for the SHOP switch, where it named the wrong unit. Here it names exactly the desktop's unit. |
| `The online store closes, every shop stops taking orders on every channel and at the counter till, and every Meituan shop closes within about a minute. Orders already placed are not affected. · 线上商城将关闭，所有门店的所有渠道及门店收银停止接单，美团各门店约一分钟内关闭。已下单的订单不受影响。` | **composed by Claude.** Built from the shop confirm (`该门店的所有销售渠道将关闭，门店收银台停止销售`), its `美团约一分钟内跟随`, and the desktop toast's `约一分钟内`. |

The last sentence states the server's behaviour: the master does not write channel cells. |

The order-import clause is the reason this confirm exists: the Eleme daemon's whole loop stops, so orders already placed on Eleme are not imported either. |

lines below needed more than a split. Each was **assembled, 2026-10-01, by

  three paths.
- **The recap** (vwRecapSentence). Its pieces are bilingual, but the verb
  ("get") and the money ("¥10 off") are English only.

## The checkout receipt's notice line (§422)

**Customer register, 2026-10-03.** The checkout receipt, mini app
(`miniapp/pages/checkout`) and web shop (`public/shop.html` `coNoteTag`). Under
a product that carries an add-to-cart notice, a box shows the notice's title
and a link that opens the full card. The title is the tenant's own words; the
card's only chrome is the live `知道了`.
